# Progress Tracker — Form-Builder SaaS

**This file is the single source of truth for "where are we right now."** It must be kept up to date and must be updated with a clear handoff note any time work is interrupted, paused, or a session ends before a milestone is finished.

## Standing Rules for This Project

1. **Always maintain this progress tracker.** Update "Current Phase" / "Status Summary" as work completes, and always write a dated entry in "Notes / Handoff" before stopping work for the session — even (especially) if the task was interrupted mid-way. Never leave the repo in a state where the next person/session has to reverse-engineer what was in progress.
2. **One standard design system, no exceptions.** Every page (builder, dashboard, submissions inbox, settings, public form runtime) uses the same shared app shell, component library, and design tokens (styles, buttons, forms, lists, inputs, etc.) — see Main Feature #6 in the plan and the future UI/UX Design System Reference (doc #19). No page invents its own one-off layout or component styling. Any exception requires an explicit, documented rationale, not a default under time pressure.
3. **Styling default — don't re-ask (confirmed with the user 2026-07-05).** Do not ask "backend-only / minimal-unstyled vs. fully styled?" per increment. The default is **every page is built fully styled, assembled from the shared design-system components**. The only increments with no styling work are those with **no pages at all** (a pure data-model / API / backend step). The bare pages parked in B1/B2b/B2c (login, register, password-reset, invite-accept, super-admin console, 2FA setup) are brought up to standard in Increment C, which builds out the shared component library itself (only `Button` exists in code today; the color/border/radius/type tokens are complete). Earlier increments were unstyled only because the component library didn't exist yet and styling then would have been rework — not because styling was ever optional.
4. **End every session with a save + a next-prompt guide (confirmed with the user 2026-07-10).** When a session is completed (or told to stop/pause), before signing off: (a) **save state to all relevant MD files** — this tracker (Status Summary + "Next Session — Resume Here" + a new dated "Notes / Handoff" entry), the auto-memory (`MEMORY.md` snapshot + any affected memory file), and any `docs/**` / ADR / plan file actually changed this session; touch only what changed. (b) **Always hand back an explicit, copy-paste "what to prompt next" guide.** For phased/increment work that means the exact next step (e.g. ``Read PROGRESS.md and build Increment F5``) with a one-line note of what it does plus any alternative tracks, and the same prompts mirrored into the "Prompts to resume next session" list below so the file and the chat never disagree.

- [x] **Phase 0 Increment A — Tenancy + RLS (2026-07-05, branch `increment-a-tenancy-rls`; verified green on real PostgreSQL via Docker Compose — 21/21 suite, fail-closed + FORCE proven red-then-green).** The crown-jewel increment: the tenant-isolation machinery every later increment sits on. Built:
  - **`meridian_app` role (the linchpin)**: a **non-superuser, NOBYPASSRLS** role that **owns** the tables and is the app's runtime connection. RLS is ignored for superusers, and a table owner bypasses RLS unless `FORCE` is set — so making `meridian_app` the owner means the fuzz pack proving "A can't see B" *is* the proof FORCE is active. Created in `docker/postgres/init/01-create-testing-db.sql` (local) and a CI provisioning step; `.env.example`/`config/database.php` default `pgsql` → `meridian_app`, plus a `pgsql_privileged` (superuser) connection for seeding platform-global rows.
  - **`app/Support/Tenancy/TenantIsolation.php`** — RLS policy generator, SQL-generation split from execution. Emits all **four policy shapes**: strict-equality + nullable-global (both fuzz-tested now), and `users` join-shape + belongs-to-me + draft-guard (emitted + unit-tested; behaviorally fuzzed when their tables land in B/D). Encodes the non-negotiables once: `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and the fail-closed two-arg `current_setting(...,true)` form.
  - **`withTenantIsolation()`** global helper (autoloaded via composer `files`) — the one call every tenant-scoped migration ends with; **`app/Support/Tenancy/TenantContext.php`** (set_config, transaction-scoped `applyLocal` for tests/jobs + session-scoped `apply`/`forget` for HTTP; clears to SQL NULL, never `''`, to stay fail-closed); **`BelongsToTenant`**/**`TenantScoped`**/**`HasUuidv7`** concerns; **`EstablishTenantDatabaseContext`** middleware (registered as the `tenant.context` alias — attached to routes in B; sets both `app.current_tenant_id` and `app.current_user_id`).
  - **`scripts/migration-lint.php`** (new CI gate, `composer run migration-lint`) — fails any migration that declares a `tenant_id` column without calling `withTenantIsolation()`. **Proven red-then-green locally.**
  - **Harness tables** (throwaway, like `SkeletonProbe`): `tenants` (RLS-exempt central table), `probes` (strict), `global_probes` (nullable-global) + models. **`tests/Feature/Tenancy/CrossTenantIsolationTest.php`** (the fuzz pack: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE isolation, fail-closed, FORCE metadata, ORM-scope-agrees-with-RLS, nullable-global read + write-refusal, non-superuser guard) and **`tests/Unit/TenantIsolationSqlTest.php`** (8 pure SQL-shape tests, green locally).
  - **CI**: `static-analysis` gains migration-lint; `tests` provisions `meridian_app` + a `meridian_testing` DB it owns and connects as it.
  - **Verified green on real PostgreSQL (Docker Compose, 2026-07-05)**: `docker compose up` → `meridian_app` confirmed non-superuser/non-BYPASSRLS and owner of both DBs → `artisan migrate` as `meridian_app` (probes/global_probes show `relrowsecurity`+`relforcerowsecurity`, 8 correct policies) → **`php artisan test` = 21/21** (the 10-test fuzz pack included). **FORCE proven red-then-green** (commenting out the FORCE line → 7 fuzz tests fail as the owner bypasses RLS → restore → green); the migration linter was likewise proven red-then-green. Also green on the host: `composer run quality` + the SQL unit suite.
  - **Bug caught by the live run + fixed**: a cleared custom GUC reads back as `''` (empty string), not `NULL`, and `''::uuid` errors — turning fail-closed into a hard failure. Fixed by wrapping every policy read in `NULLIF(current_setting(...), '')::uuid` so both "never set" and "set-then-cleared" map to NULL ⇒ zero rows. (This is exactly the kind of runtime-only defect the Postgres run exists to catch; the static/unit gates could not have.)
  - **Deviation from the approved plan — stancl/tenancy deferred to B**: the plan assumed "v4," which **does not exist** (latest stable is v3.10.0). Since stancl only provides tenant *identification* (subdomains/auth), which isn't exercised until B and can't be verified without a running app, and A's DoD is fully met by the machinery above with our own `Tenant` model, the dependency is deferred to B (where it's wired end-to-end). Nothing built in A depends on it.

- [x] **Phase 0 Increment B1 — Auth foundation + identity + user-level RLS (2026-07-05, merged to `main` via PR #2 `e4253fa`; verified 31/31 on real Postgres locally + CI).** The auth layer + real identity tables + the user-level RLS shapes A left emitted. Built:
  - **Packages**: Fortify 1.36 (session auth) + Sanctum 4.3 (tokens) + **stancl/tenancy 3.10** (single-DB). stancl configured `bootstrappers => []` (RLS is the isolation, not per-tenant DB swapping); the `TenantCreated → CreateDatabase` job pipeline pruned from `App\Providers\TenancyServiceProvider`. `App\Models\Tenant` extends stancl's base with a **UUIDv7 id generator** (`app/Support/Tenancy/Uuid7Generator.php`) + explicit `getCustomColumns()`.
  - **The crux — RLS-on-`users` vs. login bootstrapping**: the join-shape `users` SELECT policy fails closed with no user/tenant context (exactly the state during login/registration/password-reset). Solved with a dedicated **non-superuser `meridian_auth` role** + **`pgsql_auth` connection** + **`app/Auth/RlsAwareUserProvider.php`** — resolves users on the pre-auth connection (permissive `TO meridian_auth` SELECT, `users`-only), resets the authenticated model back to `meridian_app` so no elevated connection leaks into request code, and keeps the credentials lookup on `pgsql_auth` so the unauthenticated password-reset save works. `meridian_auth` created via a privileged, guarded migration + `docker/postgres/init`.
  - **Identity/schema**: `users` → UUIDv7 PK + Fortify 2FA cols + `is_super_admin` + ToS/privacy consent + soft-deletes (`sessions.user_id` → uuid); new `tenant_users`, `user_ui_preferences`, `personal_access_tokens(+tenant_id)`; `tenants` gains `owner_user_id`/`status`/stancl `data`; the stancl `domains` migration re-dated (uuid `tenant_id`) and added to the migration linter's `EXEMPT_TABLES` (it's the pre-context tenant lookup).

    - **invite** — reserve a role on a `tenant_users` row + a hashed, opaque token (7-day expiry); create a placeholder user or reuse the existing global identity (resolved on **`pgsql_auth`** — the join-shape `users` RLS hides a non-member from the inviting Admin, same cross-RLS lookup `CreateNewUser` uses); reactivate a prior declined/removed row rather than duplicate it (writes wrapped in a txn, notify after commit). **Owner is never invitable.**

    - **decline** — record declined, grant nothing.

    - **transferOwnership** — one txn: repoint `tenants.owner_user_id` (central, RLS-exempt), promote the incoming member to Owner, demote the outgoing Owner to Admin (never left roleless; the outgoing owner is an active member ⇒ resolvable on the default connection, not `pgsql_auth`). ## Notes / Handoff

*(Newest entry on top. Every entry: date, what was in progress, what's left, any blockers.)*

- **2026-08-15 (Phase 4 — LANE B, `P2c`: the ADR-0002 §D5 constraint-boundary gate; MERGED (PR #155 → `e949930`, 6/6 with every job's `conclusion` AND `steps` count parsed individually — 11–20 steps each, none empty))** — Took the queued row "the ADR-0002 §D5 boundary linter". **Verifying it against the code changed the increment, ninth time running: the row aimed the whole thing at unique indexes, and P2a had already built that gate a day earlier.** The half §D5 names *first* had never been measured. Live catalog: **113 foreign keys, of which 29 point at a `tenant_id`-carrying table without carrying it in the key**, against 9 using the composite `(tenant_id, x_id) → (tenant_id, id)` shape. PostgreSQL documents that referential-integrity checks *always bypass row security*, so the constraint layer is the one place this schema's backstop is structurally absent — and **20 of the 29 are `ON DELETE CASCADE`, making it a cross-tenant WRITE rather than a dangling read.** Delivered as gate-and-record (scope agreed with the user up front): a reasoned constant with a rationale per entry and a 60-character floor, a drift test asserting both directions against `pg_index`/`pg_constraint`, and a host-run AST linter that names the migration line the catalog cannot. **ADR-0002 §D5 amended in place rather than a new ADR**, which also allocated no number while the 0017 collision was live. **`ADR-0002`'s Consequences section asserted "no cross-tenant foreign keys or unique constraints (D5)"** as a property that keeps extraction workable — corrected, keeping the half that is true (no such reference *exists* in the data; what is false is that the schema prevents one). Same failure class as P2a's `Dedicated db | In effect: Yes` and P2b's `0700`. **CI: Pest 4073 / 17,233 assertions, reconciling EXACTLY at +6 tests / +6 assertions against base `a5cea89`'s own green run (4067 / 17,227)** — 7 new cases less the 1 moved out — predicted before the run and matched to the digit; third increment running that this has closed first try. Gates: lint 93/101/29 + 115 checked / 0 unreadable · PHPStan 18 phantoms, zero non-phantom · `openapi.json` byte-identical · Pint passed · gitleaks 24 findings, **zero tracked**. **What is left for Lane B: the threat model's still-owed SSO section (§8 has authentication rows since J3c1 and no SSO rows at all), then CRDT sync.** Remediation of the 26 fixable FKs is filed in `docs/feature-backlog.md` with its real cost — eight parent tables need a `(tenant_id, id)` unique, `forms` ↔ `form_versions` is circular — and three of the 29 cannot be fixed that way at all, having no `tenant_id` on the source. **Lessons, and the two sharpest are about the gates rather than the schema.** (1) **The adversarial pass ran after 6/6 was green and found BOTH gates blind in the same place** — the linter judged foreign keys on the SOURCE table, so it never examined the exact three constraints the constant calls its centrepiece, proven by removing each and watching the script hold exit 0 while the drift test reddened; and the drift sweep expanded `indkey`, which carries `INCLUDE` columns as well as key columns, so a covering unique would have read as compliant — **the tell was `with ordinality` computing an `ord` that nothing used.** Fourth increment running that this pass has earned its place, and 14 findings were each verified against the live catalog before acting rather than taken on trust. (2) **A gate must print what it EXAMINED, not only its verdict** — a dropped-table pre-pass skipped all 101 migration files while exiting 0, and the only thing that revealed it was the pass line reporting how many constraints it checked (zero). (3) **Three recorded reasons were factually false**, the worst being `permissions_name_guard_name_unique` filed under "secrets" when `permissions_tenant_insert` permits a tenant-owned row today and, unlike `roles`, its unique does not lead with `tenant_id` — the one live defect in the list, now recorded as such. (4) **The planning census ran against a database two migrations stale**, putting 42/112 into an ADR where the truth is 43/113; the crossing counts were right only because they came from the drift test, which runs under `RefreshDatabase`. Second time this has bitten (P2a was first). (5) **The base was RED on arrival and another session fixed it independently the same day** — J3c2 had staled P2b's extract census; #154 landed the same repair while this branch carried its own, so the duplicate was dropped in a rebase and the more conservative of the two `state_id` judgements was taken. **A red base is inherited by everyone and owned by nobody.** (6) `phpstan clear-result-cache` is required after `composer install`, or a stale-vendor analysis is served from cache — it read 31 errors where the truth was 18. (7) An empty `gh pr checks` meant CONFLICTING, not a broken pipeline.

- **2026-08-14 (Phase 4 — LANE B, `P2a`: isolation tiering; MERGED (PR #150 → `1aa906d`, squash + delete branch, all 6 CI green with real steps))** — Took the queued row "dedicated-database tenancy" and **could not build it as named, which is the finding.** Three exploration agents and three design agents were run against the code before planning; the row's own foundations turned out to be fiction in four places. **CI: Pest 3926 passed / 16,781 assertions (2 warnings, pre-existing in `StructuredRuleEvaluatorTest`, verified on a stashed tree), E2E 533 passed / 3 flaky / 10 skipped / 0 failed (17.1m), Storybook axe 229 across 34 suites, Static + Contract + Frontend green.** Four commits: the guards, the corrections, the ADR, and one CI fix that was not mine to need.

  **WHY THE ROW IS FORECLOSED, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT EFFORT.** (1) **Identity is resolved before any tenant exists** — Fortify routes `/login` with `domain => null`, and the `pgsql_auth` connection exists precisely because the join-shape RLS on `users` fails closed pre-context; at the moment of login there is no subdomain and therefore no tenant database to look a person up in. One human also belongs to several workspaces, so per-tenant `users` means N password hashes and N TOTP secrets for them. (2) **Three RLS policies subquery a neighbouring table** — `users`→`tenant_users`, `resource_grants`→`forms`/`scope_nodes`, draft-children→`form_versions` — and PostgreSQL has no cross-database subquery; a policy whose referent is absent does not fail closed, it **errors on every SELECT**. (3) Production is **one box with one PostgreSQL instance** (ADR-0005), so a dedicated database buys blast-radius containment and not the word — and **not residency at all**, which needs a region and is a hosting decision. **ADR-0017** therefore decides isolation *tiering* with the runtime default unchanged, names **schema-per-tenant in the same instance** as the target, and rejects database-per-tenant on the record. It also records that schema-per-tenant is **not** the "one uncommented line" `config/tenancy.php` implies: stock `PostgreSQLSchemaManager::makeConnectionConfig()` **replaces** `search_path` rather than prepending, dropping `public` and with it the `geometry` type, `users`, `tenants`, `jobs` and the `migrations` table.

  **TWO LIVE DEFECTS, BOTH FOUND BY THE NEW GUARDS ON THEIR FIRST RUN, AND BOTH INVISIBLE TO GREP.** (a) **The admin console had been telling operators dedicated-DB tenancy was live.** `TenantDetailPresenter::features()` *generates* its table from `plans.feature_flags` and labels unknowns with `ucfirst(str_replace('_',' ',$key))`; `EntitlementService::feature('dedicated_db')` resolves true on Enterprise and `ToggleableModules` does not list it — so every Enterprise tenant saw `Dedicated db | Plan grants: Yes | In effect: Yes | Note: —` beside capabilities that genuinely work. Because the row is generated, the search a reader runs before concluding "nothing consumes this key" finds a seeder, a docblock and one negative unit test, and never the surface. `PlanCatalog`'s **seeded, rendered** Enterprise description compounded it. This is P1c's "a test pins copy, not truth" recurring one increment later, in a place no test could have been written because nobody knew the sentence existed. (b) **`Tenant` had been serving a stale `updated_at` since the model was written.** `created_at`/`updated_at` were missing from `getCustomColumns()`, so VirtualColumn's `encodeAttributes()` copied them into the `data` blob on save and `decodeVirtualColumn()` set them back **over** the real column on read; Eloquent stamps `updated_at` *after* the `saving` event that encodes, so the copy is always one save behind (measured on the dev database: column 19:54:38, blob 19:54:11). `created_at` escaped notice for a year only because it never changes. **The whitelist alone does not heal an existing row** — the decode loop iterates the keys *present in* `data` — hence migration `2026_08_16_000001`, cast through `jsonb` because the column is `json`.

  **`domains` CARRIES `tenant_id NOT NULL` AND HAS ZERO RLS POLICIES**, deliberately: it is the table read to decide which tenant a request *is*, so scoping it by tenant is circular. It is also exactly the case `scripts/migration-lint.php`'s own `EXEMPT_TABLES` comment denied existed. The consequence is why `TenantScopedTables` holds classification as **data with a rationale** rather than as a derived rule: any future code reasoning "carries `tenant_id`, therefore RLS is filtering it" reads every tenant's hostnames, custom domains and verification tokens. Classification is a *decision*, and no query separates "unprotected because somebody reasoned about it" from "unprotected because somebody forgot" — so the list carries the reasoning and `TenantTableClassificationDriftTest` carries the drift, in both directions.

  **THE REVERSE DIRECTION EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY, AT MY EXPENSE.** It failed naming `sso_auth_failures` — a table P1c itself added — because my catalog sweep had run against `meridian`, a dev database never migrated past P1c. **Every total I had reported was one short.** The authority is `meridian_testing` after `RefreshDatabase`: **55 base tables · 169 policies across 41 tables · 40 carrying `tenant_id`**. The unique-index sweep was wrong the same way twice: `pg_constraint` alone misses **partial** uniques, which Laravel emits as bare indexes with no constraint row, so the real count is **10** — not the 6 a design agent predicted nor the 7 I first measured.

A J3b archive entry documented a test fixture by reproducing its literal value, which is itself a `generic-api-key` match on a line carrying no directive. J3c1 diagnosed that exactly right, added the allow-directive to the archive line — and then wrote a Current Status paragraph *explaining* the diagnosis that reproduced the value again, on a line that again carried none. So the branch stayed red, in a different file. **P2a went red having introduced nothing**, established by scanning three ranges in order: the 24 changed files (clean), the P2a commit range (clean), Lane A's `c94ba81..ceb1448` (two findings, both the same value). A rebase did not help, because the fix carried the defect forward. **Prose about a scanner is still input to the scanner** — the rule is not "document the match", it is "never write the value without the directive on the same line". Fixed in Lane A's block, which Rule 7(d) reserves to them; stated in the commit rather than done quietly, because the alternative was leaving the shared integration branch un-mergeable for both lanes over one token. Verified with gitleaks **8.21.2**, the version CI pins, across all 1,865 tracked files.

  **THE PEST DELTA RECONCILES EXACTLY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE RULE.** 3926 against `ceb1448`'s **3863** is **+63**, and the four new test files plus one added console case are exactly 63 (46 · 7 · 5 · 4 · 1). P1c's +29 was recorded as unreconciled because it was compared against a base two merges stale; this one was compared against a run of the **same base** and closed on the first try.

A test asserting the empty GUC would fail here while being true in production, and the tempting "fix" would pin the harness's behaviour as though it were the product's.

(2) **computed write-back = persist + index.** **Engine (both mirrors):** new tokens `+ * / >= <=` (the lexer already had `-`); new `ArithmeticNode` + `ArithmeticOperator` (add/sub/mul/div); parser precedence chain inserts additive < multiplicative < unary-minus below comparison (`-<number>` still folds to a negative literal for v1.0 byte-compat, `-<operand>` lowers to `0 - operand`); `ComparisonOperator` gains `Gte`/`Lte` (evaluator `numericCompare` refactored to take the op; **structured conditional rules can now use gte/lte too** — a bonus, and it keeps the `conditionForOperator` match exhaustive); `FunctionRegistry` opens `if/3`, `count/1`, `int/1`, `today/0`, `now/0` (parser gains a general `parseCall` + per-function `validateCallArgs`; `selected` keeps its bespoke string-literal-arg path); `FunctionCallNode.kind()` is now name-dependent (Value for the value-functions, Boolean for `selected`/`contains`). **Evaluator semantics (total over data):** arithmetic coerces both operands via `toNumber`; a NaN operand (empty/non-numeric) OR division by zero → NaN, **normalised to `null` at the value boundary** (a blank computed value) + `toBool(NaN)=false` (new guard); `count(x)` = array length (repeat instances / multi-select) / 0 empty / 1 non-empty scalar; - **2026-07-07 (Follow-up fix — tenant routes on the central host redirect to the app home instead of 500ing; MERGED to `main` PR #16 `421d103`)** — While testing the merged app locally the user hit a raw 500 (`NotASubdomainException`, "Hostname localhost does not include a subdomain") at `http://localhost:8080/dashboard`. **Root cause is pre-existing, NOT from Increment E** (verified: the E merge touched none of `routes/tenant.php`, the tenancy middleware, or `config/tenancy.php`): `/dashboard` is a tenant-**subdomain** route, and `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/the apex are central domains with no subdomain, so `InitializeTenancyBySubdomain::makeSubdomain` returns `NotASubdomainException`. Behavior chosen with the user (redirect-to-central over a bare 404). **+2 tests** (`tests/Feature/Tenancy/CentralHostFallbackTest.php`, `actingAs()` so the request reaches the tenancy pipeline); **150/150 Pest**, `composer run quality` green, no API-spec change; all 6 CI jobs green → squash-merged (`421d103`), branch deleted, local `main` synced. **The demo tenant is reachable at `http://acme.localhost:8080` — log in there and use `/dashboard`; bare `localhost:8080` is the central host** (`*.localhost` auto-resolves in most browsers; otherwise add `127.0.0.1 acme.localhost` to hosts). Known rough edge left for later: Fortify's post-login redirect to `/dashboard` isn't tenant-subdomain-aware, so logging in on the central host now lands on the central Welcome rather than the dashboard — a Phase-1 UX polish if wanted. No blockers; next = the deferred form-engine spike (ADR-0004) or Phase 1.

## 2026-07-16 — G8b (offline outbox + Background-Sync replay + media queue + authenticated sync API) MERGED (PR #40 2b476e1)

Built the offline engine on the G8a shell. Dexie DB (4 stores) as the client source of truth; one framework-free `replayOutbox(db,fetch)` shared by the app driver (`useSyncOutbox`, triggered on online/visibility/manual "Sync now") AND the service worker (switched `generateSW`→`injectManifest`, `sw.ts` owns a Background-Sync `sync` handler for no-tab replay; classic bundled `sw.js`, WebWorker-lib `tsconfig.sw.json`). `RuntimeSession.submit()` enqueues to the outbox first (durable intent) then replays inline/queues; `201/200`→synced, `422`→needs_attention, `409`→conflict (G8c), network→retry w/ 5-attempt escalation; media uploads first + placeholder-ref rewrite. UUIDv7 client ids; autosave localStorage→Dexie `draft_answers`; `device_id`/`app_version` wired through `SubmissionPayload`→`persist()` + guest request/controller. New Group-B sync API: `GET /api/v1/sync/manifest` + batch `POST /api/v1/sync/submissions` (per-item results); guest PWA replays via guest endpoints. plainClone() fix: reactive proxies can't be structured-cloned into IndexedDB. Gates: Vitest 404, Pest 759, vue-tsc (app+SW), classic `sw.js` build, Redocly+no-drift, Pint/controller-gate/migration-lint; Larastan phantom-only locally (CI-green). Next = G8c (409 conflict-resolution UX).

## 2026-07-16 — G8c (409 conflict-resolution UX + answers-content-checksum conflict) MERGED (PR #41 6211916)

The last G8 slice; **G8 (PWA/offline) is now COMPLETE**. Two forks landed together (user-chosen): the conflict-resolution UX AND the optional answers-content-checksum 409. **Frontend (reuse the fill screen):** the parked `outbox status:'conflict'` rows (flagged by G8b's replay 409) get a **Review** CTA on `SyncStatus.vue` (`ConflictReviewKey`); `App.vue` `beginConflictReview()` re-mints + re-fetches the current schema and remounts `RuntimeSession` seeded with the saved answers (existing `restoreAnswers` drops stale keys + mints a fresh uuid) + a resolve notice — the same online-drift machinery from a parked-row entry point. Successful resubmit discards the old row (`discardConflict`); a "discard this response" hatch exists. `RuntimeSession` gains a `resolving` mode that suppresses autosave (new `enabled` guard on `useAutosave` — the durable copy is the outbox row) and hides `SyncStatus`. New: `listConflicts(slug)`, `nextConflict()`/`discardConflict()`; `conflict_code` on `OutboxRow` (non-indexed → no Dexie bump). Interactive resolution is current-form-slug-scoped (App's single share-token client is bound to `bootstrap.slug`). **Backend (content-checksum 409):** nullable `submission_answers.answers_content_checksum` + `AnswersContentChecksum` (canonical SHA-256, key-sorted, list-order-preserving); `SubmissionPipeline` hashes the normalized answers and, on a duplicate `client_submission_uuid`, compares stored-vs-incoming → match/null = the existing 200 no-op, differ = new `SubmissionConflictException` → **409 `submission_conflict`** (distinct from the version-drift `submission_version_superseded`; batch `sync/submissions` maps it per-item). **Narrowing:** no server-side merge (409 body omits the server's answers) → resolution resubmits the user's LOCAL copy as a fresh response. Gates: Pest 769 (+10), Vitest 414 (+10), type-check/build(sw.js)/Pint clean, OpenAPI no-drift, e2e conflict Review→resubmit→drains + axe. Larastan phantom-only locally (pre-existing `$user->id` param-type). CI 6-green on #41. Next = G9 (question library / templates).

## 2026-07-17 — G9a follow-up: post-merge review of PR #42 + hardening fixes

Post-merge review of the merged G9a diff (~2,577 lines / 37 files). **Verdict: the security-critical parts are correct** — `withTenantIsolation(...,'nullable_global')` emits the shared `TenantIsolation` policy SQL (no hand-rolled policies); cross-tenant instantiate 404s at route-binding time (the `{template}` binding resolves on the tenant connection, so class-level `can:create,Form` is sufficient); `saveAsTemplate` with no tenant context fails closed (`NULL = NULL` is NULL, not true); `FormTemplate` correctly omits `BelongsToTenant` per the `GlobalProbe` rationale. Findings were hardening/efficiency, none a live vulnerability.

**Fixed:** (1) `PlatformRowCounter` — the only request-reachable `pgsql_privileged` (superuser, RLS-bypassing) path in `app/`; the platform-row invariant lived only in the caller's PHP `tenant_id === null` check, so it now carries `whereNull('tenant_id')` in the query itself plus a `COUNTABLE` table/column allowlist; `config/database.php`'s "never used by request code" comment was stale (true until G9a) → rewritten to name this standing exception. (2) `TemplateGalleryPresenter` + `FormTemplateResource` no longer decode `schema_blueprint` in PHP just to count fields: new `FormTemplate::scopeWithoutBlueprint()` (card columns + `COALESCE(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(...)='array' THEN jsonb_array_length(...) END, 0) AS field_count`) + `FormTemplate::fieldCount()` (prefers the projection, falls back to the in-memory blueprint for the freshly-created `store` row). The web gallery's `->get()` was unbounded and hydrated every blueprint. (3) `SchemaBlueprintMaterializer::materializeInto()` `$actor` made non-nullable — `form_fields.created_by` is NOT NULL, so the `?User $actor = null` default was a guaranteed 23502 raw QueryException past the fail-closed `BlueprintValidator` (and a trap in G9b's path; `materializeField` already required an actor). (4)+(5) Documented, not changed: the platform `usage_count` bump runs on a separate connection so it autocommits outside `instantiate()`'s transaction (accepted — a cosmetic counter drifting +1 on a rolled-back instantiate); and the API's `usage_count`-led cursor pagination can skip/duplicate mid-walk (accepted for a browse gallery).

**Dropped after investigation:** `BlueprintValidator` doesn't enforce `form_field_validations_rule_xor_chk` (exactly one of `expression`/`rule_type`) — unreachable today: no endpoint accepts a raw blueprint (`StoreFormTemplateRequest` takes only `form_version_id` + meta), save-as always round-trips through `SchemaSnapshotSerializer` reading valid rows, and `PlatformTemplateBlueprints` holds **zero** validations and is materialize-tested by `PlatformTemplateSeedTest`. **Flagged for G9b** — hand-authored library questions with validations are exactly the ingress that makes it reachable. Also dropped: `can.use` is always true (route + presenter compute the same `can:create,Form`), harmless as a future entitlement seam; and per-table RLS test duplication (the shapes are proven in `CrossTenantIsolationTest`).

**+4 tests → Pest 794 (0 fail).** The tenant-row guard test writes tenant + template on the **privileged** connection so it proves the guard bites rather than passing on row-invisibility (a row written on the app connection sits unseen inside `RefreshDatabase`'s transaction, and the test would pass for the wrong reason); **verified by mutation** — deleting `whereNull('tenant_id')` fails it. Gotcha found: `Tenant::on('pgsql_privileged')` is silently ignored (stancl's base model pins the central connection) → use the query builder. Larastan **77 errors before == 77 after** (all pre-existing elsewhere; 0 on touched files); Pint/controller-gate/migration-lint pass. Verified against real seeded data: all 10 platform templates' SQL `field_count` matches the PHP truth (4–7 fields each) and the blueprint never enters the model.

## 2026-07-18 — G9b Question Library (`field_library`) BUILT on branch `g9b-field-library` (PR pending)

Second half of G9. The builder's Fields ⇄ Library loop + `/api/v1/field-library`, on G9a's proven nullable-global plumbing — **no new infra**. New `field_library` migration (data-dictionary §11: nullable-`tenant_id` + `withTenantIsolation(...,'nullable_global')`; `is_active` + the per-field `field_type`/`default_label`/`default_config`/`default_validations`, no `schema_blueprint`) + `FieldLibrary` model (NO `BelongsToTenant`, like `FormTemplate`/`GlobalProbe`). Two mappers: `toBlueprintField()` rebuilds the 21-key `SchemaSnapshotSerializer` field shape from the stored columns (synthesizing defaults for the ~14 it doesn't persist) so `materializeField` can insert it; `fromField(FormField,$meta)` captures a draft field back into columns via a new public `SchemaSnapshotSerializer::snapshotField()` and **drops cross-field validations** (a non-null `related_field_key`) so a library question stays portable.

Reuses G9a's `SchemaBlueprintMaterializer::materializeField` (the single-field entry point written for exactly this) + `PlatformRowCounter` (now allowlists `field_library`) + `BlueprintValidator`. Two `FormBuilderService` methods: `insertFromLibrary` (mirrors `addField`: `DB::transaction` + `lockDraft` + `resolveDraftSectionId` + `materializeField` + `bumpLibraryUsage`; calls `BlueprintValidator::validateField` first because `materializeField` — unlike `materializeInto` — skips the validator) and `saveFieldToLibrary` (mirrors `TemplateService::saveAsTemplate`, `assertDraftChild`-guarded, tenant_id explicit). Collaborators resolved via `app(...)` inside the methods so the constructor-less `final` service keeps every `new FormBuilderService()` call site working.

**Carried-over #43 fix landed:** `BlueprintValidator` now enforces `rule_xor_chk` (exactly one of `expression`/`rule_type`) on both `validate()` (whole-form) and a new single-field `validateField()` — G9b's seeded/hand-authored validations are the first blueprints that make that DB CHECK reachable as a raw 23514 instead of a clean `FormException`.

Web (builder CSRF fetch sidecar): 3 routes under the builder block, all `can:update,form` — `POST fields/from-library`, `POST fields/{field}/save-to-library`, `GET library-items` — + `FormBuilderController` methods returning the same `presenter->field()` shape as `storeField` (store merges it exactly like `duplicateField`). Picker data ships as an **Inertia prop** on the Builder page (`BuilderPresenter::libraryList()`, active-only, popular-first) because the sidecar has no GET; a `builderClient.get` + the GET route were added for post-save/cross-session refresh. Vue: left-pane **Fields ⇄ Library** toggle (`aria-pressed`, not a tablist — no tabpanel to wire) + new `LibraryPicker.vue` (own + platform, "Meridian" badge, name filter, `MdsEmptyState`), store `insertFromLibrary`/`saveFieldToLibrary`/`refreshLibrary` (+ `library`/`librarySaved` state), and a one-click **Save to library** in `ConfigPanel`'s Advanced tab (names the item from the field label; transient confirmation, auto-cleared).

API (Group B): `GET/POST /api/v1/field-library` reusing `READ_FORMS`/`WRITE_FORMS` (no new ability/policy, no `can:` — not a bound model); lean `FieldLibraryResource` omits the jsonb; `store` authors from explicit attributes (jsonb cols default `{}`/`[]`, never null). `openapi.json` regenerated (+2 paths); `OpenApiContractTest` now asserts `/field-library` **and** `/form-templates` (closing the G9a in-suite gap). Seeder `PlatformFieldLibrarySeeder` upserts **6** platform questions (`Data\PlatformFieldLibraryItems`: full name, age, sex, phone, email, consent) on `pgsql_privileged`, idempotent on name, drift-guarded by `PlatformFieldLibrarySeedTest`; wired into `DatabaseSeeder` + `E2eSeeder`. Capital-`D` `Data` dir per the Linux PSR-4 gotcha.

**+24 tests → Pest 818 (0 fail, full Docker suite):** `FieldLibraryRlsTest` (RLS enabled+forced, no-author-global QueryException, read own+platform, no-update-global no-op), `FieldLibraryMapperTest` (fromField drops cross-field rules, toBlueprintField defaults, full round-trip), `FieldLibraryBuilderTest` (insert appends + usage bump for tenant AND **platform** via the privileged path, save-from-label, `childNotInDraft` guard), `FieldLibraryApiTest` (list omits jsonb, author 201, forbid read-token, reject bad field_type — uniquely-named `fieldLibraryAdmin()` helper), `PlatformFieldLibrarySeedTest` (6 validate+materialize + idempotent), `BlueprintValidatorTest` (XOR both/neither/exactly-one + validateField tolerates unresolved related_field_key), + `field-library-axe` Playwright spec. Host gates green: Pint, vue-tsc (app + SW), phpstan level-8 on changed files (`-d memory_limit=3G` — fixed 3 real errors: `findOrFail`→`whereKey`+`firstOrFail` for a single-model return, dropped a redundant `is_string`, `array_values(...)` for a `list` return), controller-gate, migration-lint. **`npm run build` + Vitest can't run on the Windows host** (only Linux `@rolldown` bindings + skipped bin-links) — CI-only; vue-tsc proved the TS/Vue compiles. Ships **ungated** (consistent with G7/G9a). Narrowing: no standalone "manage library" screen (the `is_active` toggle + rename-after-save are deferred). **MERGED — PR #44 `eb6bda7`, all 6 CI jobs green.** The E2E job took 3 test-only follow-ups: (1) a `/Full name/` `getByRole` matched 3 buttons because the seeded "Community Health Survey" already has a "Full name" field → scope the picker locators to `.library`; (2)+(3) the whole-page picker `assertClean` re-flagged a pre-existing borderline `target-size` on the toolbar's `.builder__back` at the tablet viewport (a surface builder-axe already gates at all 3 widths, yet passes) → **scope the new picker's axe scan to `.builder__pane--left`** rather than re-scan shared chrome (min-height on `.builder__back` was tried first and reverted as out-of-scope + ineffective). Lesson: a new interactive-surface axe spec should `.include()` only the NEW UI.

## 2026-07-20 — G10b1: grant + hierarchy write surface (backend + /api/v1) — MERGED, PR #46 `35a0d3a`, all 6 CI jobs green on the first push

Decomposed G10b into **G10b1 (backend + API)** / **G10b2 (UI)** with the user, alongside three other decisions taken up front: **one node per form** (keep the `forms.scope_node_id` pointer — a pivot would rewrite G10a's tested resolver core); **fix the over-broad form list in this increment**; and **one** new `manage:scopes` ability mapped to both `scopes.manage` and `forms.collaborators.manage`.

**`ScopeNodeService` gained `update`/`setActive`/`delete`/`move`/`deletionImpact`.** The keystone is `move()`, and the plan's original locking spec turned out to be insufficient: `FOR UPDATE` on node + target parent leaves a real hole, because a concurrent move of an **ancestor of the target** re-paths the target without locking it — the first mover then grafts its subtree onto a stale prefix, and `path` is exactly what authorization prefix-matches, so a corrupted path is a corrupted permission. Fixed with a **transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed on the tenant** (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(class, crc32(tenant))` — the two-int form rather than the undocumented internal `hashtext`; `_xact_` so a crashed request cannot strand it). It is the only advisory lock in the codebase — every other service serializes on a row (`forms`, `submissions`) — because it is the only operation whose correctness spans an unbounded row set rather than one aggregate root. The `FOR UPDATE` re-reads stay and still do work the advisory lock doesn't (authoritative post-lock rows; blocking a concurrent rename/deactivate of the two endpoints). Then: a **one-line cycle check** (`str_starts_with($target->path, $node->path)`, which covers move-onto-self because `path` is self-inclusive, and which is now the **only** thing preventing a longer cycle — `scope_nodes_no_self_parent` only ever covered the single-node case, so that migration's now-false comment was corrected); a depth cap measured across the **whole subtree** (a shallow node can carry a deep one); and a **single** `UPDATE` re-path over the constant-prefix `LIKE` — atomic (no window where a concurrent read sees a half-grafted tree), index-served by `(tenant_id, path)` under `COLLATE "C"`, one statement whatever the subtree size.

**`ScopeNode::booted()` was KEPT VERBATIM rather than relaxed.** The guard covers Eloquent *saves*; the re-path is a query-builder statement that fires no model events, so the invariant "no model save ever touches `parent_id`/`path`/`depth`" survives intact while the one audited writer sits behind the locks. An `unguarded`/re-entrancy flag was considered and rejected: it converts a structural invariant into something any future caller can switch off. The G10a test asserting model-level re-parenting throws is kept green as the proof, and a new test re-asserts it *after* `move()` ships.

**A genuine PostgreSQL trap, found by running the tests:** `substring(path from ?)` with an untyped bind parameter resolves to the POSIX-**regex** overload `substring(text, text)`, which returns NULL when the pattern doesn't match — it would have nulled `path` on every row it touched. The NOT NULL constraint turned it into a loud failure; fixed to `substr(path, ?::int)` with both numeric binds cast explicitly, and documented, because the same trap in a nullable column is silent data loss.

**New migration `2026_07_21_000001`** adds two CHECKs that make an incorrectly re-pathed row impossible *regardless of which writer produced it*: `scope_nodes_path_self_suffix_chk` (`path LIKE '%/' || id || '/'`) and `scope_nodes_depth_matches_path_chk` (`depth` = slashes minus 2; the design draft had minus 1, which would have rejected every valid row — verified against real values before writing it). The second also forces `path` and `depth` to be written in the same statement. Validated by `migrate:fresh` + the full suite, including `ScopeNodeScaleTest`'s hand-composed bulk rows.

**Node deletion now removes the subtree's grants in-transaction.** `resource_grants` is a morph with no FK, so nothing cascaded them and every node delete silently manufactured orphaned authorization rows. This is cleanup at the site that creates them, *not* the deferred orphan sweeper. Uses a SUBQUERY, not a `whereIn` over collected ids (PG caps binds at 65535; a PSGC region is ~44k nodes).

**New `ResourceGrantService`** — upserts so a demotion editor→reviewer **replaces** rather than accumulates (the unique key deliberately excludes `capacity`); re-resolves and **locks** the tenant-scoped target so concurrent grants cannot 23505-race and so `associate()` can never carry a cross-tenant morph pair; refuses `includes_descendants` on a form target ahead of the CHECK; `TODO(audits, Phase 1)` markers. **New `ResourceGrantPolicy`**, registered explicitly (an unmapped model class falls through to Gate closures — it fails **open**), carrying the escalation rules: base `forms.collaborators.manage`, **no self-grant** (self-*revoke* stays allowed — de-escalation), and **anti-amplification** via a new `ResourceCapacity::anyPermission()`. Rule 3 is **unreachable under the shipped 5-role matrix** (Owner/Admin are the only holders of the base permission and hold both `.any`s); that is stated in the policy docblock, in RBAC §8.4, and tested against directly-constructed permission subsets rather than seeded roles — specifically so it is not filed as dead code the way `forms.collaborators.manage` itself was for three increments.

**`ResourceGrantResolver::nodeReach()`** is the blast-radius counter, and it lives on the resolver rather than as a parallel query so the preview and the grant cannot disagree — it is the number an administrator makes an escalation decision on. Returns `{direct, descendant}`, reports **zero for a deactivated node or one under an inactive branch** (otherwise it advertises access the resolver will refuse to honour), and counts through the same `withTrashed()` scope the resolver itself uses. `escapeLike()` was made public so `ScopeNodeService` shares one escaping rule instead of copying an authorization-critical one. Also **documented and tested the `forget()` asymmetry**: the per-user variant clears only `$sets`, leaving `$formPaths`/`$inactive` stale, so `move`/`setActive`/`delete` must all call the argument-less `forget()` — a same-request-only failure of exactly the shape the G10a walkthrough caught.

**The form-list leak was fixed on BOTH surfaces.** A design pass surfaced that `GET /api/v1/forms` (`FormApiController::index`) had the *identical* "every non-archived tenant form to anyone passing the read gate" behaviour as `FormPresenter::list()` — fixing only the presenter would have moved the leak to the API rather than closed it. Both now scope via `grantedFormIdsQuery($user, ResourceCapacity::Editor)` when the viewer lacks `forms.edit.any` (Editor specifically: this is the authoring list, so a bare reviewer grant should not surface a row with every `can` flag false). All 230 pre-existing Form tests passed unchanged, plus a new 7-test `FormListScopingTest` covering both surfaces.

**API:** `manage:scopes` + 6 new paths — `/scopes`, `/scopes/{scopeNode}`, `/scopes/{scopeNode}/move` (deliberately separate from PATCH: a locked operation with its own refusals, and folding it in pushes the controller toward the complexity gate), `/scopes/{scopeNode}/impact`, `/resource-grants`, `/resource-grants/{resourceGrant}`. **Every route pairs `ability:` with a `can:` policy gate**, which is precisely what makes the single coarse ability safe — the ability map's any-of semantics would otherwise let a `scopes.manage`-only principal reach the grant routes. That constraint is recorded in `ApiAbilities::MANAGE_SCOPES` and api-spec §2.6 as a rule future routes must honour, and is asserted by a test that hand-mints a token carrying an ability its holder could not have requested (`createToken()` does not run `intersect()` — that happens in the mint controller) and shows the policy gate still refuses.

**+64 tests → Pest 966** across `ScopeNodeMoveTest` (13), `ScopeNodeMoveLockingTest` (6, deterministic lock-shape via `DB::listen`), `ScopeNodeLifecycleTest` (13), `ResourceGrantServiceTest` (13), `FormListScopingTest` (7), `ScopingApiTest` (12). Host gates: Pint green, controller-gate green, migration-lint green, **Larastan 0 errors on every G10b file**, vue-tsc green, Redocly valid, `openapi.json` regenerated (23 paths) with **no drift**. **The end-to-end walkthrough was run and all 18 checks passed** — a 4-level tree, a reviewer grant on an interior node with descendants, a subtree move between regions, an intermediate-node deactivation, the escalation refusals, and deletion impact — the exercise that in G10a found the bug the tests missed.

**Documented narrowing:** concurrent-move coverage is the deterministic pair (lock-shape + a sequential mutual-move test proving the decision is made on **re-read** state), not true two-session contention. `RefreshDatabase` wraps each test in an uncommitted transaction so a second connection cannot see the fixtures, and the suite has no committing-Feature-test precedent to follow; shipping a flaky race test was judged worse than shipping an honest narrowing. Ships **backend-only** — no `tenant.php` routes, no Vue, no Playwright, all G10b2.

## 2026-07-21 — G11: richer personalization (accent / text-size / dyslexia font) — PR #48, all 6 CI jobs green

The last increment of Phase 2, and mostly an exercise in *executing* a spec that already existed (PRD Feature #9, DSR §2.9, data-dictionary §19) — except that three of the things the spec and the tracker asserted turned out not to be true.

**The tracker's premise was wrong.** PROGRESS said "the columns already exist (C2 shipped `theme_mode` + `accent`), so this is not a schema increment." The only migration for `user_ui_preferences` shipped `theme_mode` alone; `accent` was a hardcoded `'blueprint'` literal in `User::uiTheme()` that had never touched the database. The claim traced back to the G-map plan's exploration notes, which had read data-dictionary §19 — the *target* schema — rather than the migration. General lesson worth keeping: **§-numbered docs describe intent; migrations describe reality.** Building on the stated premise would have skipped the migration and produced a feature that silently discarded every choice but theme.

**The shipped accent was broken, and structurally unobservable.** `[data-accent='teal']` had a blue hover (`--mds-primary-700`) on a teal button, no `-bg-active`/`-tint` override, and no dark variant at all — and because `[data-accent]` carries the same specificity as `[data-theme-mode='dark']` but sat later in source order, teal *won* in dark mode and painted light `#1B5E5E` on the `#123350` ground: **1.74:1** for both `action-primary-fg` and the focus ring, against minimums of 4.5 and 3. It survived two increments for a simple reason: **nothing in the product could set `data-accent`, and no test had ever set it.** The fix extended the ramp from one step to seven and verified all 17 resulting pairings independently; teal is never worse than Blueprint at the equivalent role and is better in dark (its hover clears 4.82:1 where Blueprint's fails at 3.96:1). The dark payload is now defined once as private `--mds-_accent-teal-dark-*` customs that both dark selectors assign from — the neutral dark block is *already* copy-pasted across the explicit and `prefers-color-scheme` sites, and adding a third was the obvious future divergence.

**The documented type-scale rule could not ship.** §2.9 specified "+2px per level, never changing line-heights". Holding line-height constant while growing font-size doesn't preserve a ratio, it destroys one: at extra_large that yields `body-sm` as 17px text in an 18px line box (1.06) and `caption` at 16-in-16 (1.00) — clipping descenders and failing WCAG 1.4.12. An accessibility feature shipping an accessibility regression. Replaced (user decision) with proportional ×1.125/×1.25 scaling of both properties, font-size rounded and line-height then *derived* from the role's original ratio — independent rounding would have compressed `caption` from 1.333 to 1.286. §2.9 was rewritten with the authoritative table and the reasoning.

**What the plan got right, and it mattered:** the reflow risk looked like the hardest part and wasn't. `.app-shell__content` is `overflow-y: auto`, which makes the other axis `auto` too, so it is its own scroll container and page content never reaches the document overflow chain the E2E measures. Only `TopNav` was exposed — ~344 of 375px at extra_large, about one long tenant name from failing. Hardened, plus an `overflow-x: clip` belt on `.app-shell` that makes document-level horizontal overflow structurally impossible.

**Restraint that paid for itself:** zero touches to `packages/design-system/src/components/**`. The accent picker is a label-only segmented control — a colour swatch would be a colour-*only* signifier (WCAG 1.4.1), and the control already previews the accent for free because its selected chip is painted with `--mds-color-action-primary-bg`. The dyslexia toggle reuses `MdsCheckbox` rather than building the specified-but-unbuilt `MdsSwitch`, whose own DSR row requires visible text anyway — i.e. a checkbox with extra steps. That kept the DSR §1.2 governance gate and the flakiest CI job out of the diff entirely. `ThemeQuickToggle.vue`'s diff is literally zero lines: `useThemePreference()` survives at its exact C2 signature as a mode-only facade.

**The anti-clobber guarantee is server-side.** Every rule on `UpdateAppearanceRequest` is `sometimes`, so an absent key is never validated and never reaches `updateOrCreate` — the quick toggle's `{theme_mode}`-only PATCH cannot wipe the other three axes even from a stale client. Verified by mutation: making one column write unconditional fails the partial-PATCH test exactly where expected.

**Four new guard suites make the hand-authored CSS mechanically checkable** — `type-scale` re-derives all 44 declarations from the token JSON, `theme-overrides` asserts the duplicated dark blocks stay identical (catching the pre-existing neutral copy-paste risk as a bonus), `token-references` resolves every `var(--mds-*)` in the tree, and `useTheme` pins the "default = absence of the attribute" convention. The dead-token sweep folded in at the user's request found **16** undefined tokens across 10 files, not the 2 the tracker had flagged — and it was load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the ones without fallbacks were invalid at computed-value time and inherited instead, so they'd have scaled by inheritance rather than by type role under `data-font-size`. Sites *with* fallbacks were collapsed to the fallback actually rendering, since re-pointing them to the intended colour is a design change with contrast implications, not a cleanup.

**The E2E found a real bug that no unit test would have — and it was not in G11's code.** Running the new spec locally at 834px, `extra_large` plus the dyslexia face gave the page **50px of genuine horizontal scroll** (`window.scrollTo(500,0)` really moved it). Each axis alone was fine; only the combination reached it. The diagnosis was the interesting part, because two plausible assumptions were both wrong: the `overflow-x: clip` belt on `.app-shell` made **zero** difference (identical with `visible` and `hidden`), and `body.scrollWidth` was a clean 834 while only `html.scrollWidth` read 884 — every overflowing element sat correctly inside the table's own `overflow-x: auto` wrapper. The culprit was `.mds-table__sr`, the visually-hidden "Actions" label: `position: absolute` inside a `position: static` scroll wrapper, so its containing block resolved *outside* that wrapper and no amount of ancestor `overflow` could clip it — an absolutely positioned box is clipped by its containing block, not by whichever ancestor happens to scroll. A 1px span past the last column was extending the document's scrollable width. One line (`position: relative` on `.mds-table__scroll`) fixed it. It is a latent `MdsDataTable` bug that personalization only made reachable by widening tables, so it was fixed at source rather than papered over per page — and it is the increment's single touch to `src/components/**`, which the DSR §1.2 governance gate accepts because the DSR is updated in the same commit. Locally verified afterwards: **114 E2E runs green** (18 personalization + 60 responsive + 36 public-runtime/templates).

**OpenDyslexic is the system's first webfont** and costs nothing on the default path: browsers fetch a `@font-face` src only when a rule using the family matches, and the only such rule is attribute-gated, so a user who never opts in downloads zero font bytes. It lives in a new `fonts.css` imported only by the admin app — putting it in `theme-overrides.css` would have shipped it to the guest bundle, which imports that file.

Gates: Pest **1001** (+13), Vitest **457** (+43), Pint / controller-gate / migration-lint green, PHPStan **0 on every G11 file**, vue-tsc clean, no `openapi.json` drift.

**CI needed two follow-up fixes, and both were harness-shaped — the two jobs actually feared passed first time.** `design-system-a11y` (story attribute leakage across the shared preview iframe) and `e2e` (the font-loading race and 375×extra_large reflow) were called out as the top risks and both went green on the first run, so the mitigations were the right ones. What broke instead:

1. `token-references.test.ts` threw `ERR_INVALID_URL_SCHEME` on CI while passing locally. The suites run under `environment: 'happy-dom'`, whose DOM `URL` global shadows Node's, and resolving a five-level **directory** URL (trailing slash) through it does not preserve the `file:` scheme — its two sibling suites use the identical `import.meta.url` pattern and passed, because they resolve concrete **file** paths. Switched to `process.cwd()`, which under Vitest is its config file's directory.
2. The new guest-shell test threw `Vite manifest not found`. It is the only test in `GuestRuntimeTest` that renders the shell rather than hitting a JSON endpoint, hence the only one evaluating `@vite`, and the Pest job builds no assets. It had passed locally purely because assets happened to be built — a silent local/CI divergence. `withoutVite()` (the existing convention), verified by deliberately moving `public/build/manifest.json` aside to reproduce the CI condition rather than trusting the fix.

Both are now recorded as standing gotchas.

## 2026-07-21 — G10b2: the scoping hierarchy UI (MERGED, PR #47 `ae14bc2`) — G10 COMPLETE

The UI half of G10b, over the backend merged in G10b1 — and the increment that finally makes the Reviewer role assignable by a human: build a hierarchy, assign forms to it, grant a teammate access to a whole branch. **Two user decisions up front:** ship as ONE PR (the backend carries every security-critical decision and is already CI-proven, so the risk is review size, not correctness); and the form→scope picker **requires `scopes.manage`**.

**Designed with a 12-agent workflow** (3 competing architectures → 3 deep dives → a verifying judge → 4 adversarial critics). The judge verified 35 load-bearing claims against real source — `axe-core` 4.12.1, the `@inertiajs` dist, `@vue/runtime-dom`, Laravel's exception handler — and **five were false**, three of them in the direction that would have shipped a bug: `nested-interactive` cannot fire on a `treeitem` (its matcher keys on `childrenPresentational`, which `treeitem` lacks), so one agent's "blocking finding" had deleted the drag grip and rewritten both keyboard specs against a design built on a non-sequitur; `vue-tsc` does accept custom properties in an object `:style` (`CSSProperties` declares `` [v: `--${string}`] ``); and Vue does **not** strip a `false` aria attribute, so the omit-on-leaves rule was right for a reason nobody had stated correctly.

**The merge-blocker came from an adversarial critic, not the design pass:** axe's `getOwnedRoles` pushes any child carrying a role, a **global `aria-*` attribute**, or focusability as an *owned* child of `role="tree"` rather than recursing past it — so the assertive live region and the empty state had to be **siblings** of the `<ul>`, and the scan target became `.scopes__pane`, not the `.scopes__tree` PROGRESS had specified. A second critic inverted the transport reasoning: `preserveState: true` is **already the default** for post/patch/delete, so hardening mutations was a no-op while the genuinely unsafe path — a GET visit for selection — would have remounted the page, collapsed the tree and dropped focus to `<body>` on the page's most common interaction. Selection became local state.

**Transport is forced, not stylistic.** `bootstrap/app.php`'s `$isApi` keys on the `api/v1/*` **path**, and Laravel runs custom render callbacks before JSON negotiation, so a refused move on a web route returns a 302 with a flash toast **even to an XHR** — `builderClient` would see `response.ok`, skip its guarded branch, and throw a raw `SyntaxError` parsing HTML. Every mutation is therefore an Inertia visit; the only fetches are the two read-only sidecars.

**Two real bugs the E2E found that no unit test would have.** Grab-mode entered from the detail panel's "Move…" focuses the *row*, whose keydown was still doing tree navigation — so the move could be started but never aimed. And the outcome was announced from `onSuccess`, but a no-op or refused move returns props identical to what is already rendered, so the reference watcher never fired: the announcement went silent **and the tree stayed stuck in grab mode**. Settled from the refreshed props with an `onFinish` backstop. Both were only reachable by driving the real widget.

**A day lost to a stale Vite dev server** is worth recording: the container's `npm run dev` does not see host file edits through the WSL2 bind mount, so it served a cached module and three separate "bugs" were phantoms. Stop the `node` service, delete `public/hot`, and build inside the container (`docker compose run --rm --no-deps node npm run build`) — which is what CI does anyway.

**Gates:** Pest **988 (+22)**, Vitest **414 unchanged**, Pint / controller-gate / migration-lint green, PHPStan **0 errors on all G10b2 files**, vue-tsc clean, **no `openapi.json` drift** (tenant-web routes are outside the surface). New `scopes-axe` **24/24 across all three viewports**; `/scopes` added to `responsive-axe` (6/6). `E2eSeeder` gains a **5-level** hierarchy — deliberately deeper than the minimum, because a shallow fixture leaves the 375px overflow case unreachable and makes `responsive-axe` a false negative — plus forms at differing depths, a deactivated branch, a second **ACTIVE** member and a descendant-inclusive reviewer grant.

**Local-environment caveat, verified not a regression:** `builder-axe` fails locally with `color-contrast` in a theme/viewport combination that changes between runs, and it fails **on `main` at `ca92379` too** (checked out and re-run to confirm). CI is green on main; this is a local rendering artifact.

**Narrowings:** the tree ships whole, capped at 2,000 nodes with an honest notice (expand-on-demand is the follow-up for a ~44k-node PSGC shape); grants are managed per node only. Found and deliberately **not** folded in: `--mds-color-text-muted` and `--mds-type-heading-sm-*` do not exist and are referenced at 4+ live sites.

**Merged with all 6 CI jobs green, after two fixes for failures this branch did not cause.** `composer audit` broke on three guzzle advisories published the same day (`<7.15.1`: host-only cookie scope, unbounded response cookies, Proxy-Authorization forwarded to origin) — bumped 7.13.2 → 7.15.1, transitive via `laravel/framework`, no constraint change. `npm audit --audit-level=high` then broke on `brace-expansion` and `shell-quote` DoS advisories reachable only through `@storybook/test-runner`; plain `npm audit fix` cleared both, and the 8 remaining moderates sit below the gate.

The Pest failure was the **known-flaky tampered-token test**, and it was worth fixing rather than re-running: `GuestShareTokenServiceTest::tamperSegment` flipped the LAST base64url character while calling itself deterministic, but a 32-byte HMAC is 42.7 six-bit groups, so the trailing character carries 2 padding bits and several distinct trailing characters decode to the same raw bytes — the "tamper" could leave the signature intact. It flaked once locally and once on CI the same day. `GuestRuntimeTest` already carried the first-character fix for exactly this reason; the unit helper had been missed. **The repo now has no known flaky test**, and that gotcha entry has been retired.

**E2E passing on CI is also what settled the local `builder-axe` `color-contrast` failures as environmental** — they reproduce on `main` at `ca92379` and not on CI's Linux runner.

## 2026-07-21 — G11 MERGED (PR #48 `506ff97`) — Increment G and PHASE 2 COMPLETE; Track B (Windows Server host) deferred by user decision

`gh pr merge 48 --squash --delete-branch` against head `7fe07be`, all 6 CI jobs green. `main` fast-forwarded `2c9bede..506ff97`; branch `g11-personalization` deleted. 56 files, +2349/−144. **With it Increment G (G1→G11) and Phase 2 (Kobo-style rigor + offline) are COMPLETE** — the roadmap table's Phase-2 row is now ✅ and Phase 3 is marked ⏭️ NEXT.

**One process note worth keeping:** head at merge time was `7fe07be`, a docs-only PROGRESS.md commit pushed after the run PROGRESS recorded as green (`de599f2`/`1603c6b`). That commit triggered a *fresh* CI run which was still in-flight when the session opened, so `mergeStateStatus` read `UNSTABLE` and three jobs read `pending`. Waited for it rather than merging on the older green run or forcing it — the standing "CI green is the source of truth" rule means green **on the commit you are merging**, and a docs-only diff is not a licence to skip that. It went green in ~8 minutes (E2E is the long pole at 7m34s).

Recorded in PROGRESS.md's "Next Session" section, and the "Alternative track" line — which had offered Track B at the top of every session — was rewritten so it is no longer surfaced as an option. **Nothing is blocked:** the deploy *pipeline* has been committed and dormant since 2026-07-04 — `deploy.ps1` at the repo root plus `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, whose `if:` requires the repo variable `DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'` (never set), so it skips on every green `main` today. §8 is only the one-time box topology. ## 2026-07-21 — H1a: ADR-0007 (async execution substrate) + 12 doc reconciliations — MERGED (PR #49 `0d9df25`), docs-only, PHASE 3 BUILDING STARTS

**Phase 3's entry point, on the G5a/ADR-0006 docs-only precedent (PR #32 `d2a3ff7`): retire a cross-cutting design fork in a reviewable document before any code depends on it.** Six of Phase 3's twelve verticals dispatch jobs and every rollup/reaper/sweep in the phase is cross-tenant — a pattern with no precedent in the codebase — so the async contract had to exist before H2. The audit (three Explore agents, every `file:line` re-read against source) found the foundation is **almost entirely prose**: exactly one queued job (`ScanAttachmentJob`, `final`, defining none of `$queue`/`$tries`/`$backoff`/`$timeout`/`failed()`/`middleware()`); no worker or scheduler service anywhere (the only committed worker invocation is `queue:listen` in `composer.json`'s `dev` script); no scheduler at all (`routes/console.php` is 8 stock lines, no `withSchedule`, no `app/Console/`) against **four documents asserting one**, most bluntly `feature-backlog.md:85`'s *"scheduler + email + async export already exists"*; and `onQueue(` with **zero hits** against a five-name queue catalog documented as binding in two places.

**The keystone: a live defect two documents called "Mitigated".** `TenantContext::$tenantId` is a process-lifetime PHP static; `applyLocal()` scopes only the *database* GUC to the transaction and `set()` assigns the static unconditionally, with nothing rolling it back — and there is no `Queue::before`/`JobProcessing` listener anywhere. On a long-lived `queue:work` worker the GUC therefore goes NULL while the static still holds the previous tenant, so `BelongsToTenant` injects it into the next context-less job's reads and auto-fills it on `creating`. RLS still fails closed, so the practical effect is zero-row reads and confusing `QueryException`s rather than cross-tenant disclosure — but ADR-0002:125 and security-threat-model:40 both promised *"fails fast (explicit exception)"* and it did not, and it escaped notice only because no second job type exists. ADR-0007 §D4 closes it; both documents were corrected to cite the mechanism rather than assert an unbuilt one.

**ADR-0007 is `D1…D13` and deliberately departs from ADR-0006's skeleton (user decision): no weighted scorecard.** ADR-0006 scored a *spike* with measurements; this ADR has none, and §D9's rate ceilings are explicitly unvalidated planning assumptions on a queue nothing has ever consumed — a rubric would have manufactured false precision. It uses ADR-0005's plain drivers + Concern/Choice table with ADR-0006's `**DN — …**` bullets and `**Method note.**`, which states plainly which parts are audited evidence and which are reasoning. **D1** is the `database` driver on Postgres with a plain `queue:work`, **superseding ADR-0005 rows 27–28 in part** — the repo's first *row-level* supersession, chosen over amendment because it is the honest description and avoids retiring an otherwise-live ADR (the whole-ADR precedent, ADR-0005→ADR-0003, was followed for wording across title/Status/Related/References). Redis+Horizon is named as a non-blocking upgrade path with an explicit revisit trigger, not a rejection. **D8** decides `after_commit => true` here but implements it in H2, resolving the tension between the docs-only precedent and not specifying a rule the ADR leaves broken — it closes a real bug where `AttachmentStorageService:82` dispatches outside any transaction, letting a worker beat the row and strand `virus_scan_status` at `pending` forever, structurally untestable under `sync` and therefore under every current CI job. **D10** refuses a fairness table because both escapes are worse than the problem (RLS in the job-reservation hot path is a self-inflicted R9; an `EXEMPT_TABLES` entry repeats the `failed_jobs` hazard). **D12** records a constraint no document stated: any tenant-facing failure surface is itself a cross-tenant read of an RLS-free table, sanctioned only via `pgsql_superadmin` + `superadmin_bypass`.

**Verification caught six citation defects in the source plan before they were written into the corpus** — `handle()` is a `function (): void {}` closure, not `fn() =>` (syntactically impossible for a statement list); "no guzzle / no Redis" was false (guzzle is transitive at `composer.lock:802`, Redis exists in infra) and was narrowed to *no first-party outbound call site* / *no Redis-backed queue in use*; `horizon:terminate` is **not in `deploy.ps1`** at all, only in `deployment-infrastructure.md:43`, so that correction stood but inverted; migration-lint's Rule 1 is `:105-117`, not `:99`; `TenantInvitationNotification` interpolates at `:33-35`, not `:44`; and the webhook retry ladder lives at §1 `:13`, not §4 `:49-61`, so the unbuilt banner was retargeted to the doc head (user-approved). **Two H-map claims were refuted and deliberately not written:** the *"RBAC docs say a catalog of 27 permissions"* correction is wrong — `multi-tenancy-rbac-design.md` §5 already enumerates 28 and `:112` names `scopes.manage` as the 28th, while §3's "fixed catalog" refers to the five **roles** — so writing it would have *introduced* an error, and the R6 dangling-pointer fix was substituted as the tenth reconciliation; and the *"PRD lists 8 roadmap items"* claim is unfounded (the 12 is verbatim at `PRD.md:405`; the 8 came from PROGRESS.md itself). **Two further defects found during verification were folded in:** ADR-0002:76's dangling `[D7]` anchor (the section is D6) and technical-architecture §5 layer 5, which described a "job middleware" that was never built.

**R6 is now RESOLVED** following the R7/R11 strike-through precedent. It had carried three mutually contradictory commitments: a mitigation citing §7.4, which is webhook reliability and contains no rate-limit mechanism (a dangling pointer); a §5 claim that limiter buckets were already per-tenant, untrue of the HTTP limiters as built (`AppServiceProvider:105-127` keys on token-hash/IP, deliberately, since `throttle:api` sorts ahead of auth); and an NFR deferral of per-tenant limiting to "Phase 2–3 … not before". All three are corrected, and §D9 replaces them with job middleware counting executions rather than requests.

**Next: H2** — the async substrate proper, with ADR-0007 as its specification. The single highest-value test is one integration test driving a real `queue:work --once` under `QUEUE_CONNECTION=database`: it is the only way to exercise serialize → enqueue → reserve → unserialize → context-re-entry, the path `sync` structurally cannot reach, and the only thing that would catch a regression in §D2/§D4/§D5 or the §D8 dispatch race.

## 2026-07-23 — H9a (server-side draft substrate)

H5c merged (squash → PR #56 `a65437d`; entitlement track COMPLETE); H9a built on `h9a-draft-substrate`. The H-map's next move: the server-side DRAFT substrate shared by save-and-resume (H10) + OCR (H18/H19). Backend-only — no route, no feature gate, no openapi change; the suite stays inert. **The linchpin:** a draft is written repeatedly under one `client_submission_uuid` with changing content, so the pipeline's same-uuid-different-content **409 is SUSPENDED for drafts and RE-ARMED on promotion.** New **`SubmissionDraftService`** (singleton seam, not only a route — an OCR job stages a draft with no guest request/uuid): **`saveDraft()`** runs Stage-1 normalize + the Stage-2a published guard, SKIPS Stage-3 + the 409, find-or-creates by uuid (first save creates a `status=draft` row stamping `completeness_percent`/`last_saved_at`/`draft_expires_at=now()+30d`; later saves OVERWRITE in place under `lockForUpdate` + a `status===Draft` re-check; a 23505 create-race folds into update = last-writer-wins). **`promote()`** runs the FULL Stage-3 EXACTLY ONCE (before any txn, so a failure leaves the draft resumable), flips the SAME row `draft→submitted` in place (stable `submissions.id` for H9b's resume token; source preserved; `draft_expires_at` nulled), and fires `SubmissionCreated` once (so H5b metering counts a draft only on promotion). **Re-arm is automatic** — the finalized row stores `AnswersContentChecksum::of($normalizedDraftAnswers)`, byte-identical to `submit()`, so a later same-uuid replay is the ordinary 200/409. **Stage-4 tail extracted into `SubmissionFinalizer`** (media re-point + `submission_answers` upsert + typed/geo index + `created` audit), reused by BOTH `submit()` and `promote()` — **`submit()` stays byte-identical** (proven by `SubmissionPipelineTest` passing unmodified); `create`→`updateOrCreate` for the answer doc. Alter-only migration adds the three per-SUBMISSION columns (no RLS re-emit, no status CHECK, migration-lint skips it). New pure **`DraftCompleteness`** (relevance-unaware %; excludes note/page_break/calculated/hidden; repeat section = one unit; div-0→0). **Decisions:** in-place promotion; stamp-once expiry; preserve source; double-promote = idempotent no-op; leave `submit()` byte-identical (a same-uuid finalize goes through `promote()`, never `submit()`). Gates: Pest +17 (`SubmissionDraftServiceTest` 11 incl. the HEADLINE + `DraftCompletenessTest` 6) with `SubmissionPipelineTest`/G4/G5/G6/`AuditSitesTest` regression (80) green unmodified; PHPStan L8 at the 77 local baseline (none in new files); Pint/migration-lint/controller-gate/job-payload-lint green; no openapi drift. Narrowings → H9b/H10: resume token + pre-RLS verify middleware + Group-C/B routes + draft-expiry reaper (needs H3, should hard-delete for the softDeletes×partial-unique-index edge) + tenant-configurable 30-day setting; H12a's `max_responses` COUNT + close predicate must filter `status != 'draft'`.

**Next: H9b** — the resume token (extends `GuestShareToken`, scoped to the draft `submissions.id`) + pre-RLS verify middleware + Group-C draft upsert/resume + a Group-B admin-draft route (OCR) + the draft-expiry reaper (`MaintenanceJob`, TTL from the 30-day default); needs H3.

**2026-07-27 — H1g MERGED (PR #70 `83c923a`, 6/6 CI green on the first run) — ADR-0009: OAuth Connector Token Custody; docs-only, H-map row 217.** Planned with 3 parallel Explore surveys (webhook vertical + async/entitlement substrate; central-domain routing + docs constraints; ADR corpus conventions + token-custody prior art), then 4 forks confirmed with the user via AskUserQuestion — the two that shaped this ADR were **the number** (ADR-**0009**, the next free one: 0009 was earmarked for the cancelled payments ADR that was never written, so the sequence gets no permanent hole; the Status block says so, keeping `0008:8`/`:152`'s back-references coherent) and **no Socialite** (a hand-rolled `ConnectorProvider` adapter over the repo's guarded `Http::` idiom, since Socialite assumes a same-host session-backed redirect and the callback here is stateless and central-domain). **The finding that drove the whole design:** the app's session cookie is **host-only** — `config/session.php:159` reads `SESSION_DOMAIN`, and both `.env.example:59` and `.env:56` set it to `null` — so a tenant-subdomain session is *not* readable on the central host where an OAuth callback must land (providers register one fixed redirect URI and reject wildcard subdomains). **Two comments in the repo assert the opposite** (`routes/tenant.php:49`, `routes/admin.php:15`: "session established centrally; SESSION_DOMAIN spans subdomains") and are wrong against the config they describe — the standing "prose describes intent, config/code describe reality" lesson, third instance. The ADR therefore reuses the one proven mechanism for this exact shape (a signed, domain-separated HMAC token verified **pre-RLS** by middleware — the guest share/resume-token pattern) as the OAuth `state`, rather than widening `SESSION_DOMAIN` (which would make every tenant's session cookie cross-host on every request to solve a problem occurring twice per connection). Ten sub-decisions: §D1 tokens are `encrypted`-cast **`text`** (the `varchar(255)` trap: the cast inflates to ~290 chars), `$hidden`, and — unlike `webhook_endpoints.secret` — **never returned in any form, not even masked**, because a connector token has no user-facing consumer; §D2 one central-domain callback per provider, outside `web` (a third-party GET has no session/CSRF token; `state` is the CSRF control the spec assigns); §D3 `state` = domain-separated HMAC (`connector-oauth-state.v1`), ~10-min TTL, claims `{tid,uid,prov,nonce,exp}`, provider-bound, **stateless and therefore replayable within TTL — accepted**, bounded by single-use provider codes; §D4 context adopted from the verified state pre-RLS + `forget()` in `terminate()` (a central-domain INSERT under FORCE RLS otherwise writes **zero rows without erroring**); §D5 return host read from the `domains` table (the `GuestDraftController::resumeUrl` precedent) and the outcome handed back as a **query parameter**, not a flash, closing the open-redirect; §D6 refresh is a proactive `MaintenanceJob` fan-out, never lazy inside a delivery; §D7 disconnect destroys local tokens unconditionally, provider revoke best-effort; §D8 least-privilege scopes stored per connection; §D9 app credentials in `.env` only + the **`APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS` gap recorded** (`config/app.php:99-106` supports `previous_keys`; the variable is in no `.env.example` and no doc, so an `APP_KEY` rotation would silently brick every stored token); §D10 a new `connection` audit alias with both token columns in `AuditRedactor`'s unconditional list, registered **in the same increment that creates the table**. Gate inherited, not coined: ADR-0008 §D7 already ratified `native_connectors` as one Starter+ flag key, seeded at `PlanCatalog.php:34,54` and consumed by nothing yet. Doc reconciliation shipped in the same PR (the H1a/H1b invariant — announce it, then do it): `docs/security-threat-model.md` §2 gains two attack-surface rows (the platform-held credential; the unauthenticated inbound callback), §5 is retitled "Webhook & Connector Security" and gains a nine-row connector table (verdicts labelled **Decided (ADR-0009)** so ratified design is never read as shipped mitigation), §9 gains residual item 8; `docs/data-privacy-gdpr-compliance.md` §7 gains the **elective** connector sub-processor bullet (metadata-by-default, revisit if a per-subscription include-answers opt-in ever ships). No code, no migration, no `ci.yml` change.
