## 2026-08-26 — `M15` (Lane B): the device-wide outbox belongs to a *visit*, not to the device — PR #207

**The row.** The last open `major` in `docs/feature-backlog.md` § *Submissions, drafts & the guest runtime*. `App.vue:460` mounts `<SyncStatus />` inside `.app-shell__banner`, **above the phase machine and outside every phase panel**, on `/f/{slug}` — a page with **no authentication of any kind** — and `listSubmissions()` is cross-form by design. On the shared kiosk hardware `lib/outbox.ts:12` names as the threat **in its own words** (*"This runs on enumerator tablets and shared kiosk hardware"*), the next respondent saw the previous one's queue tags, server references and per-row status sentences, and `outbox-status.ts:128` gave them a **Discard** that permanently deletes a stranger's unsent response **and its queued media** in one transaction.

**As built.** A *visit* — a UUIDv7 in `sessionStorage`, rotated on *"Submit another response"* and after ten minutes of **idle** — is stamped on every finalized row as `respondent_session_id`. Every read that **discloses or destroys** is scoped to it: the identified list, the badges, `listConflicts` (so neither review entry point can select a foreign row), `discardRow`, and the `aria-live` reference announcement. An earlier visit's unsent rows collapse to **one sentence carrying a count and nothing else**. `docs/adr/0021-respondent-scoped-device-outbox.md` carries the decision, the four alternatives and the cost; `docs/ux/form-filling-ux-flow.md` §7.1/§7.3, `docs/offline-first-sync-design.md` and `docs/security-threat-model.md` were annotated in the same PR.

⚠️ **THE SPEC WAS ON THE FIX'S SIDE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A CONTAINMENT AND NOT A REDESIGN.** §7.1 scopes its list to *"every submission **the respondent** has finalized"* — definite article, singular — and §7.3 specifies the persistent **app-level** surface as a **count plus a call to action** (*"1 submission couldn't be sent. Tap to review."*), not the identified list. The spec assumes one respondent per device throughout and never contemplates two, so scoping the identified list and degrading everything older to §7.3's own count shape is the reading that survives the case it did not consider. **There was no decision to overturn**: no ADR and no line of `docs/` had ever scoped the device-local outbox to a respondent, and `offline-first-sync-design.md` recorded the *opposite* as an assumption.

⚠️⚠️ **THE ROW'S DISCLOSURE INVENTORY WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE MISS WAS THE WORSE HALF — EIGHT-FOR-EIGHT ON GREPPING THE SHAPE RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE COUNT.** **Creation time is NOT disclosed**: `createdAt` is computed onto the view model at `outbox-status.ts:101` and has **zero consumers**, so it is dead code and not a leak. *"Which other forms"* is narrower than stated: the slug is never rendered as text, only as the `href` of *"Open this form"*, on a cross-form **conflict** row. But the sweep found **two exposures the row never named**. **`useSyncOutbox.conflictRow()` bypasses the answer-scrub** that `listSubmissions` performs as belt and braces (*"nothing that renders a list should be handed answer data at all"*) and hands the raw row to `App.vue:384`, which seeds a fill session with `row.answers` — so **Review rendered a stranger's ANSWERS, field by field**, two clicks from an always-visible banner, which is strictly worse than everything the row did name. And **`useSyncOutbox.ts:127-128` wrote the server reference into an `aria-live` region**, so a background replay of an earlier respondent's row read it aloud. Four of the row's six file:line citations had also drifted, every one of them because M14 grew `App.vue`.

⚠️ **VERIFYING THE ROW'S "PRE-EXISTING vs NEW" SPLIT IS WHAT SET THE SCOPE, AND IT IS ONLY PARTLY TRUE.** Review genuinely is pre-existing — `beginConflictReview`/`ConflictReviewKey` landed in **G8c (`6211916`, 2026-07-16, PR #41)** and were reachable by a second respondent from that day, because `SyncStatus` was the default landing surface. But **destroying a stranger's parked answers was ALSO already possible pre-I10d**, via Review → *"Discard this response instead"*; what I10d added is Discard **without entering a review flow**. And **the server reference did not persist on the device at all before I10d** — `markSynced()` used to *delete* the row, and I10d began retaining twenty receipts for twenty-four hours — so **the single most identifying datum in the list is new**. The practical consequence is the fix's shape: hiding the LIST without scoping `listConflicts`/`conflictRow`/`conflictHere` would have left every action reachable, which is the forced-neighbour lesson M14 paid for, one increment later.

⛔⛔ **THE OBVIOUS DESIGN IS WRONG, AND ONLY A GATE THAT CANNOT RUN ON THIS HOST SAYS SO.** The first design was a module-scope id minted per page load: stricter, simpler, nothing persisted. **`tests/e2e/public-runtime-offline.spec.ts:186` kills it** — that test queues a row, flips it to `conflict` through raw IndexedDB, **RELOADS at `:225`**, and only *then* asserts `review-conflicts` (`:233`), `/needs? review/i` (`:237`), `Retry now` count 0 (`:241`) and drives the resolve flow (`:246`). A per-load id makes that row a stranger's after the reload, `conflictHere` falls to zero, and four assertions die **at merge**, on a suite this host cannot run. The gate is right and the design was wrong: **a respondent who refreshes the page has not become a different person.** `sessionStorage` is what encodes that; the two rotations are what stop it becoming *"whoever used this tab last"*. **Grepping the merge-blocking spec BEFORE choosing a design, rather than after writing one, is the whole reason this cost nothing.**

⛔ **ONE ASYMMETRY IS THE DECISION RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT: THE DRAIN IS NOT SCOPED.** `replay.ts:158` calls `listPending(db)` and `sw.ts:80-92` calls `replayOutbox(openDb(), fetch)` with **no session, no slug and no hooks** — a service worker **has** no `sessionStorage`. A respondent-scoped drain would strand every earlier row on the device **forever**, which is precisely the silent data loss the offline architecture exists to prevent. So `retryAll` and the background replay stay device-wide, and the rule that separates them from `discardRow` is stated in both files: **sending a stranger's submission discloses nothing and destroys nothing — it is what they wanted; showing it and deleting it are the harms.** **Nothing is deleted for privacy**: an earlier visit's unsent row is hidden and still drains, `pruneSynced` still never touches an unsent row at any age, and only a delivered *receipt* is dropped — because it can never again be rendered (the list is scoped) or counted (`earlierUnsent` counts unsent rows only), so retaining it would keep a server reference on shared hardware in exchange for nothing.

⚠️ **AND THE SESSION ID IS AN ARGUMENT, NEVER AN IMPORT, WHICH IS A TYPE-CHECK CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A STYLE PREFERENCE.** `lib/respondent-session.ts` reads `sessionStorage`; `sw.ts` imports `lib/db.ts` and `lib/replay.ts` → `lib/outbox.ts`, and `tsconfig.sw.json` re-checks that graph under `lib: ["ESNext", "WebWorker"], types: []`, where `Storage` does not exist. One import would fail the second `vue-tsc` program. The id is therefore read at the composition root, provided through `RespondentSessionKey`, and crosses into the data layer as a plain string — **the shape `lib/device.ts` has always had, for the same reason**, which is why the constraint cost nothing to satisfy.

➕ **A COPY CONTRADICTION NO SUITE COULD HAVE SEEN, FOUND BY RENDERING THE HAND-OVER AT :8081.** The next respondent read *"Nothing is waiting to be sent from this device."* **directly above** *"One response from an earlier session on this device is still waiting to send."* Both sentences were individually defensible — the first is about **them**, the second about the **device** — and nothing on screen said so. happy-dom computes no layout and asserts no copy here, and no e2e assertion covers that string. **The visual pass was in the plan because the paired containment gate demands one for its own reasons; it paid for itself on something else entirely.** Now pinned by a test.

⚠️ **PAIRED FILE — STANDING RULE 7(b-bis)'s FIRST EXERCISE, AND IT WORKED EXACTLY AS DESIGNED.** `packages/design-system/src/theme/__tests__/clipped-node-containment.test.ts` lives in **Lane A's tree**, its `SCAN_ROOTS` reads `resources/public-runtime` off disk, and its `KNOWN_UNGUARDED` listed `SyncStatus.vue` under an assertion of **exact equality in both directions** — so the guard and the list entry could only ever move together, in one PR, by one author. `.sync-status` gained the `position: relative` its sr-only region had always needed (that file's only positioned rule was the clipped node itself, which the gate deliberately excludes). **The gate was proven to bite before it was trusted** — removing the declaration puts the file straight back in the offender list — **and the containing block was verified in a real layout** (`sr.offsetParent === .sync-status` on the running page, with no horizontal overflow and no page growth at 375px), rather than inferred from a green test. `RuntimeShell.vue` stays listed: this increment did not touch it, and a containing block added without a look at the running app is exactly what that file's note refuses.

➕ **FILED, NOT FIXED — AND THE BIGGER ONE IS WORSE THAN THE ROW THIS CLOSED.** `draft_answers` is keyed `[form_version_id + slug]` (`db.ts:127`) with **no respondent dimension at all**, and `RuntimeSession.vue:149-156` restores it on every fresh session under a **seven-day** TTL, with `clear()` firing only on the submit paths — so an **abandoned** mid-fill draft is restored into the next respondent's form **silently, with their answers on screen** and no banner. It is deliberately **not** M15's shape: the outbox had a spec-sanctioned degraded surface to fall back to and the draft has **no analogue**, because its legitimate feature *is* cross-visit restore; telling a personal device from a kiosk needs an operator concept the guest runtime does not have, which is the unbuilt kiosk-mode row and is therefore its precondition. Shortening the TTL is not a fix — the next respondent arrives in five minutes, not seven days. **Both it and the `reconcile.ts:43` copy defect beside it were filed the moment the decision not to fix was taken**, per the rule J4b1's four invisible defects bought.

**Gates.** **Vitest 130 files / 2,213** — `public-runtime` **35/782** (from 34/744), with **`design-system` 35/545 and `resources/js` 60/886 exactly unmoved**, measured rather than assumed · `vue-tsc` clean on **both** programs, including the service-worker one that exists to catch precisely the mistake this design had to avoid · four host lint gates **97 · 111 · 31 · 111/119/0**, exit codes read **without a pipe** · **Pest, PHPStan and `openapi.json` structurally unmovable — zero PHP files in the diff**, and the contract job confirmed it · **no Dexie `version()` bump**: the field is un-indexed, the precedent `conflict_code`/`server_reference`/`synced_at` set, and `db.test.ts` pins both `verno === 2` and the five-store list · **mutation-probed rather than assumed** — removing the `discardRow` ownership guard reddens one case, removing the `listSubmissions` filter reddens two *different* ones, and both were byte-restored and verified by SHA.

⚠️ **AND ONE SELF-INFLICTED LESSON, ONE STEP REMOVED FROM M14's.** The `resources/js` chunk came back **exit 137 with no summary** — I SIGKILLed my own run by issuing `docker restart fb-lane-b-node-1` for an unrelated inotify refresh while that chunk was executing inside it. M14's lesson was *confirm what a stray process belongs to before killing it*; the generalisation is **check what is running INSIDE a container before you restart it, not just what is running on the host**. Re-run clean.

## 2026-08-26 — 🅰️ LANE A / `M17`: the horizontal-overflow assertion, made able to fail (PR #208, `2279293`, 6/6)

**A gate that could not fail, on every `AppLayout` page, for thirty-six days.** `assertClean` measured `documentElement.scrollWidth` while `AppLayout.vue:147` set `.app-shell { overflow-x: clip }` — and `clip` mints **no scroll container**, so the number could not move. The guard now keys on the one property that causes the blindness: a shell that is specifically **`overflow-x: clip`**.

⚠️ **PLAYWRIGHT ABORTS A TEST AT ITS FIRST FAILED ASSERTION, SO EACH QUARANTINE REVEALED THE NEXT.** One test calls `assertClean` three times; the base failure hid `— Add`, which hid `— Form`. **Three CI runs to drain a test that had reported exactly one problem.** ⛔ **None was pre-listed on a hunch, deliberately:** `KNOWN_OVERFLOWING` asserts a quarantined page *still* overflows, so a speculative entry fails **exactly as loudly** as a missing one. **A symmetric list makes guessing worthless, which is the property that keeps it honest.**

⛔ **QUARANTINED RATHER THAN FIXED, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: NONE REPRODUCES ON WINDOWS.** A probe inlining OpenDyslexic as a **data URI** — defeating the recorded cross-origin font trap, `document.fonts.check()` true — measured **0 overflow across all six page × viewport combinations**, as did a plain tablet probe of the form hub. 17/24/28px is the size of **Linux-vs-Windows font metrics**. ⚠️⚠️ **THE MISLEADING COMMENTS MISATTRIBUTED REAL CATCHES, WHICH IS WORSE THAN OPTIMISM.** Two claimed specific saves — *"has now caught Domains and the Audit log"*, *"has reddened this gate three times (H12b, H14, H15b)"*. **The clip landed 2026-07-21 (`506ff97`); all three merged 07-26/07-27**, six days later, with the assertion already dead. They went red on **axe violations**, credited to the neighbour. Corrected **in place rather than deleted**: **a comment citing three specific saves is exactly what stops the next reader from testing the claim.**

⚠️ **ONE CLAIMED FILE WAS RELEASED UNTOUCHED AND THAT WAS THE PLAN.** `DnsRecordBlock.vue` was claimed *"for the MUTATION ONLY … reverted before the PR opens"* — restored from **saved bytes** (never `git checkout --`, per M9), **sha256-identical**, absent from the diff.

## 2026-08-26 — `M19` (Lane A): the four overruns the repaired gate found, and a Linux e2e loop (PR #210)

M17 quarantined five scan labels in `KNOWN_OVERFLOWING` because *"none of them reproduces on a Windows
host"*. **That reason was wrong, and why it was wrong is worth more than the three declarations that
fixed them.**

⛔⛔ **THE PROBE WAS AIMED AT A FONT THAT CANNOT REACH THE ELEMENTS THAT FAILED.** It inlined
**OpenDyslexic**, confirmed `document.fonts.check()` returned `true`, and measured 0 overflow across all
six page × viewport combinations. Both halves true; the conclusion did not follow.
`theme-overrides.css:404-406` re-points **only** `--mds-font-family-body`, and its own docblock at
`:389-395` states the Display role is untouched — while `.page-header__title` and `.builder__title` are
both `--mds-font-family-display`, and the form hub carried **no personalization at all**. The variable
that actually differs is the **display stack's platform fallback**: with `"Segoe UI Variable Display"`
absent, `system-ui` resolves to Segoe UI on Windows and **DejaVu Sans** on a CI runner, **~27% wider** —
**256px against 324px** for the word "Submissions" at 48px/750. **A probe that measures zero has told
you nothing until you know it exercised the thing that broke.**

✅ **REPRODUCED TO THE PIXEL BEFORE A LINE OF CSS CHANGED — 17 / 24 / 28, CI's three numbers exactly —
THEN 0 / 0 / 0.** Three one-line declarations, each the escape its own file already used elsewhere:
`.page-header__title` and `.mds-stat-tile__value` take `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; `.builder__title-row`

**The finding: a gate is only as narrow as the widest route that reaches the same bytes.**
`GET /attachments/{attachment}` is authorized by `AttachmentPolicy::view()`, whose entire body was
`$user->can('submissions.view')` — it never touched its `$attachment` argument. ADR-0015 §D6 filed the

`form_editor` while `feedback.view` is held by none of them. The id-addressed sibling therefore served the
PII image to exactly the three roles the dedicated route refuses — while `FeedbackController`'s own docblock
said it declined to route through `AttachmentController` *precisely to avoid that coupling*. **Live, not
latent.** `AttachmentPolicy` had no test of any kind and no HTTP test anywhere drove that route.

**The census unit has to be the RESOURCE, not the feature — M26's lesson at one more remove.** M26 learned
to enumerate consumers of a field from the code rather than the report. Not enough here: "who serves this
screenshot" finds two routes and stops. What found the defect was enumerating **every endpoint in the
repository that serves stored bytes — ten** — and asking of each which test asserts a refusal. **Four of ten
had one.** Two routes reaching the same bytes under two different permissions is invisible to any sweep
organised by feature.

**The row's own proposed fix was half-inert, and it was measured.** `SubstituteBindings` runs before
`Authorize`, so the cross-tenant `assertNotFound` the row asks for 404s at route-model binding and passes
unchanged with the middleware deleted. Mutation 3 removed that middleware and reddened the same-tenant
Viewer case alone. Both cases ship; the cross-tenant one now carries a comment saying it is not a substitute.

**Three mutations, pairwise disjoint red sets** — 1 / 2 / 1 against a green 19-passed baseline, with the
named positive control in mutation 2's set. **And the harness failed first, in the way hardest to notice:**
v1 spliced by index arithmetic and produced syntactically invalid PHP, where every test errors — which reads
as *"the mutation was detected"* if you only count red. v2 replaces one literal token per mutation and adds
two checks the standing rule does not name: **`php -l` the mutant, and assert its sha256 actually moved.**

**`TaskStop` on a background shell is not `kill` on what that shell spawned.** Stopping the harness killed
the tool's wrapper and not the `bash` script, which kept running and mutating; its `docker exec` host side
died while the container's Pest kept going, and a new PID appeared after the first kill. Three kills —
wrapper, host script, container process — before the tree could be restored.

**A namespace handed over in a next-prompt is a reservation, not a destination.** The claim reserved
ADR-0016 §D35 because the hand-off named it; ADR-0016 is SAML SSO. ADR-0015 §D6 created this coupling, §D7
already says *"both screenshot routes"*, §D8 marks the row PII — so the decision is **ADR-0015 §D9** and the
reserved slot was never spent. Seventh consecutive Lane B increment amending rather than minting.

## 2026-08-26 — 🅱️ LANE B, `M33`: the attachment id that defeated every per-form boundary (PR #221, `f329e1b`, CI 6/6 green with real step counts)

**The row.** `AttachmentPolicy::view()` required only `submissions.view` where `SubmissionPolicy::view()`
requires that permission **and** org-wide visibility or per-form collaboration or being the respondent. So
`GET /attachments/{attachment}` read **any stored object in the tenant by id with no per-form check at
all**, while every surface that *lists* those objects is scoped. Affected roles: exactly `form_editor` and
`reviewer` — `hasOrgWideVisibility()` is `dashboard.org.view`, held by owner, admin **and viewer**.
**Revocation did not revoke:** remove a `form_editor` from a form and `SubmissionPolicy` refuses them the
submission on the next request, while every attachment id they ever saw kept working indefinitely.

**As built.** An exhaustive `match` over all nine kinds with **no `default` arm**. Three kinds answer on a
permission alone because they have no form to scope to (feedback screenshot `feedback.view`; brand logo any
member — deliberately *not* narrowed, since `/branding/logo` serves the same bytes unauthenticated to email
clients; webhook envelope `webhooks.manage`). The five submission-domain kinds require the permission **and**
their owner's scope, and the submission arm **delegates to `SubmissionPolicy::view()` through the Gate rather
than copying its predicate**. `Avatar` fails closed. ADR-0015 gained **§D10**; the webhook narrowing is `D4`.

### The finding: a row's EVIDENCE and a row's PRESCRIBED FIX are separately trustworthy

**All eight of the row's citations held — the first time in fifteen increments the evidence half needed no
correction.** And its one-sentence remedy was still wrong: *"resolving each kind's owner through the morph
map"* is impossible **and forbidden**. Two of the five `attachable_type` aliases are deliberately
unregistered (registering them splits Sanctum's `tokenable_type` and Spatie's `model_type` between alias and
FQCN — the `enforceMorphMap` break that cost 90 test failures), and `BrandingMorphAliasTest` exists solely to
pin that **and prescribes this increment's design by name**. ⚠️ **Lane A independently hit the identical
shape in `M32`'s row the same day** — *"REAL, and the row's own prescribed fix does not work."* Two lanes,
two unrelated rows, one day. **Fifteen increments have taught this project to verify a row's citations;
nothing has been verifying its remedy — the half that decides what gets built.**

### What the row did not name

1. **A sixth reachable kind.** It enumerated four; a census by **resource** (every `AttachmentKind::`
   producer under `app/` and `database/`) found five production writers, including the unnamed **brand
   logo**. M29's census lesson held a second time: **the unit is the resource, not the feature.**
2. **A fixture the fix silently invalidated.** `Attachment::factory()` defaults to a `form_field` alias with
   a **random uuid**; M29's positive control used it, and under a policy that resolves the owner it would 403
   for *every* role. **A green suite after a scoping change is not evidence until the fixtures are checked
   for owners that never existed.**
3. **A link that keeps working and one that correctly stops.** `GeneratePdfJob`'s PDF-ready link resolves for
   every legitimate recipient (they passed `SubmissionPolicy::export()`); it stops only for someone since
   removed from the form — which is the defect.

### Two process findings

⛔ **WHEN YOUR ROW EXTENDS AN UNMERGED PR OF YOUR OWN, `origin/main` IS THE WRONG BASE.** M33 cut from `main`
and got **17 passed / 3 failed** on a factory method M29 adds — **the failures had nothing to do with the
diff and looked exactly like a broken test.** Re-cut from the dependency branch, after which
`git rebase origin/main` was clean in both files, and the conflict the M29 release note predicted never
happened. **Saving bytes protects you from losing work, not from having saved the wrong work:** one saved
file had to be re-derived because its copy was itself built on the wrong base.

⚠️⚠️ **TWO LANE-B WRITERS SHARED ONE WORKTREE, AND RULE 7 DOES NOT COVER IT.** `fb-lane-b` was checked out
onto a branch this session did not create, with live uncommitted edits to `PROGRESS.md` and
`docs/claims/lane-b.md`; a `gh pr merge 219` returned *"already merged"* because the other writer merged
seconds first. **The claim protocol held and the worktree did not** — that writer read the pushed M33 claim,
preserved it as the `## Status` heading, released only M29's, corrected the Pest baseline to the same figure
this session measured independently, and left an explicit rebase instruction. Nothing was lost. **But Rule 7
assumes one worktree per lane: the claim file protects the FILES; nothing protects the CHECKOUT.** Detect it
with `git worktree list` plus `git reflog` (a checkout you did not issue); the discipline that made it
recoverable is **commit and push before you switch branches**.

### 2026-08-26/27 — Lane A, `M30`: the guest limiter keyed on a parameter one of its five routes does not have (PR #220, `5e58c05`, 6/6 green)

Row: the `major` under `### Test suite & CI gates` — *the login and 2FA-challenge rate limiters are asserted
by no test*. **The row was a coverage gap and verifying it found a LIVE defect one door over.**
`RateLimiter::for('guest')` keyed its per-token `Limit` on `route('shareToken')`; measured from the live
route table, five routes carry `throttle:guest`, four declare `{shareToken}`, and
`GET /api/v1/public/drafts/{resumeToken}` does not — so `(string) null` is `''`, `hash('sha256','')` is a
constant, and **every draft-resume request in the deployment shared one 30/min bucket**. The throttle is
middleware index 0 there, so a garbage token spent the budget before anything verified it, and the per-IP
arm's 60/min let one unauthenticated IP refuse every legitimate resume link platform-wide for free.

**Neither change that caused it was wrong on its own** — F5's key was accurate when every route on the
limiter carried `{shareToken}`, and H9b's resume group reused `throttle:guest` correctly. **A limiter's key
is a contract with the route's parameter NAMES, and nothing expressed it.** Generalised: any middleware
alias reading `$request->route('<literal>')` is coupled to every route that will ever carry it, invisibly at
both ends.

**Both of the row's mechanisms were wrong on the installed framework version**, and it had inherited its
*"resolves to an UNLIMITED PASSTHROUGH"* premise from this repository's own `SsoLoginWebTest.php:286` — true
on Laravel ≤ 9, false on v13.18.1, where an unregistered limiter throws `MissingRateLimiterException`. A
test written to the row's rationale would have targeted a mutation the suite already catches. **Read the
vendor source for the version installed; a project's own comment is not a citation.**

**Four positive controls, each restored by sha256 byte comparison, and one found a vacuous test a green run
would have shipped:** the IP-fallback case's first draft was `->not->toContain($key, $message)` and stayed
GREEN with the offending key in the array, because **Pest's `toContain` takes variadic needles, not a needle
and a message.** Only reading what the control printed caught it. The structural gate **invokes** the
limiter per live route and asserts two tokens yield two keys, rather than holding its own copy of the
parameter names — which would have been 7(b-bis)'s paired-list hazard one file later.

**Protocol findings.** (a) Lane B was detected four minutes into an increment whose claim file still read
NO ACTIVE CLAIM, via `git worktree list` — **the other lane's worktree HEAD is observable when its claim
file is not**; re-reading at write time was necessary and not sufficient. (b) Lane A's forward queue
(`M31`, `M32`) was pre-claimed in writing and **Lane B read the whole file, found it, and took `M33`** —
the obvious arithmetic would have collided. (c) The first CI run was a **zombie**: queued 8h53m with no job
ever started while later runs passed; the tell is a later run finishing first, and merging current `main`
into the branch restarted it while also avoiding the force-push a rebase would have needed.

**Filed, not fixed:** `POST /user/confirm-password` carries **no rate limit at all** (`major`, live —
unlimited online password guessing on the redemption door for `RequireRecentPassword`, while SAML step-up
and `POST /two-factor-challenge` are both bounded); `throttle:saml-acs`'s route binding is unasserted; and
the false passthrough rationale in two SSO files.

after the colon discarded — and its own header says at `:33` that it "cannot judge whether an allowlisted
reason is TRUE".

### The finding: a remedy can fail STRUCTURALLY, not just narrowly

Every one of the row's citations held — the **second row running**, after `M33`. Its prescribed fix did not.
*"Copy `GET /forms/{form}/submissions/export`, which asserts BOTH a role denial and a scope denial"* binds a
**Form instance**; both analytics exports gate on `can:viewAny,SavedReportView`, whose policy method **takes
no model**. A scope denial there is not weak — there is nothing to be out of scope of. And the **role** half
needed a fixture the row never names: all five seeded roles hold `dashboard.form.view` while `viewAny` is
`dashboard.org.view || dashboard.form.view`, so **no seeded role can be refused**, and copying the row's own
viewer fixture would have produced a 200 and a green test proving nothing — **the exact failure the row was
filed about, reproduced by obeying it.** Lane A hit the identical evidence-good/remedy-bad shape in `M32`'s
row the same day. **That is now a pattern.**

Every target carries a `feature:` gate beside its `can:`; had the entitlement answered first, every new test
would have measured the plan. `route:list` resolves all three as **`ability → Authorize → RequireFeature`** —
entitlement **last**. One command, risk closed.

## 2026-08-27 — 🅰️ LANE A, `M31`: the concurrency guard that was pinned from one side only (PR #223, CI 6/6 green with real step counts)

Row: the `major` under `### Test suite & CI gates` — *every accepted write in the answer-edit concurrency
suite compares `null === null`*. **Test-only diff**; two files amended, none created.

### The headline held, the probe did not, and the damage was under-stated

`SubmissionAnswerFactory` stamps no `answers_content_checksum`, so `seedInboxSubmission()` produces the
*legacy* row, `baselineOf()` casts null to `''`, `ConvertEmptyStringsToNull` returns it to null, and all
three accepted writes reached `SubmissionAnswerEditService.php:135` with null on both sides. **Every hop the
row named was true.**

⛔ **Its prescribed probe was not.** *"Drop the client token from the guard and the suite stays fully green"*
is false: **deleting the guard reddens three cases**, because editor B re-reads the answer row at `:114`, so
the under-lock check at `:202` compares a value against itself and B's write is accepted. M30 predicted this
in its queue block and it held. **The suite was never blind to REMOVING this guard — only to WEAKENING it**,
so a test written to the row's stated rationale would have been aimed at a mutation the suite already
catches. **Second consecutive increment where that was true**, after M30's `throttle:login` rename.

### Three mutations measured, two survived, and they point in opposite directions

| Mutation | Before | After | Damage if shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| **(1)** `$baseline === null && $stored->… !== null` — presence-only | **60 passed, GREEN** | **2 failed** | Two editors each holding a real, *different* token never conflict; the lost update returns silently. |
| **(2)** `$baseline !== null \|\| $stored->… !== $baseline` — reject every non-null | **60 passed, GREEN** | **4 failed** | Every pipeline-written submission **permanently uneditable** — the row's own phrase, and the direction it never named. |
| **(3)** `answers_schema_checksum` for `answers_content_checksum` | **2 failed** | 2 failed | *Already caught.* |

⛔⛔ **(3) IS THE FINDING, NOT THE FOOTNOTE.** Because `null === null` is trivially **true**, any mutant that
breaks the equality outright throws on the accepted writes and reddens them — the adjacent-column typo, the
inverted operator, a recomputed checksum, a transformed token. **The only survivors are those that preserve
`(null, null)` equality AND `(real, null)` inequality — i.e. those discriminating on nullness alone.** That
is a far narrower and more useful statement than *"the suite compares null to null"*: **the suite pinned
exactly one bit, and the guard has two.** It also explains why the first two candidate mutations were
discarded before they were run, and why the third was run anyway — the reasoning was checked against a
measurement rather than trusted.

### Four cases, and the fix that was deliberately not made

Two per file, all through the real submit pipeline so the rows carry production-shaped checksums —
`SubmissionAnswerEditTest`'s own `submitForEdit()` helper, which the row correctly noted **no concurrency
case used**, and a sibling defined locally in the routes file. ⚠️ **Defined locally on purpose**: Pest's
helper functions are global, so calling `submitForEdit()` across files passes on a whole-suite run and dies
with `Call to undefined function` on a per-file run — the same global-namespace trap `editableIndexedForm`'s
docblock already records, arriving from the other direction.

⛔ **NOT FIXED IN `SubmissionAnswerFactory`, AND THE CLAIM REFUSED TO PREJUDGE IT.** Stamping a checksum
there would **convert** the legacy rows rather than **add** the production ones. Three reasons in increasing
order of weight: it changes the fixture shape under every caller of `seedInboxSubmission()` in **both**
lanes' suites; it deletes the only coverage the nullable path has; and **that path is a supported production
state rather than a fixture artefact** — `EditSubmissionAnswersRequest` uses `present` + `nullable`
deliberately, and says in its own words that `required` *"would make those rows permanently uneditable"*.
**The obvious "fix the fixture" move would have destroyed real coverage to buy new coverage.** The old cases
stay and still pass.

### ⛔⛔ The process finding: a positive control that failed silently, and returned GREEN

Every new case asserts its baseline is a non-empty string before using it — without which each degrades back
into a fourth `null === null` the moment the pipeline stops stamping. **Control D proves the guard fires:**
nulling `SubmissionFinalizer.php:96`'s stamp fails all four **at that assertion**, printing *"Failed
asserting that null is of type string"* and *"Expecting '' not to be ''"* against the exact lines.

**Control D's first run was a false negative and nothing in the test output said so.** The mutation was
written as `perl -0pi -e "s/…\$contentChecksum,/…null,/"` inside **double** quotes; the shell consumed the
escaping, **the substitution never applied**, and the suite returned **`64 passed`** — a result
indistinguishable from *"the guard is decorative and the control disproves it."* It was caught only because
the command **printed the mutated line** and the line was unchanged.

⚠️ **A CONTROL MUST PROVE ITS OWN MUTATION LANDED BEFORE ITS RESULT MEANS ANYTHING.** A green positive
control is either a real disproof or a no-op edit, and the test output cannot tell them apart. Every
mutation in this increment therefore greps the mutated line and aborts on no match. **This widens the
standing shell rule: it eats backticks, and it eats `\$` inside double quotes — a silently-unapplied
`perl`/`sed` mutation is a false negative that flatters the code.** Third increment running where reading
what the control *printed*, rather than its exit status, was the thing that worked.

### A second process finding: the line-count delta caught a swallowed bullet

The `PROGRESS.md` splice reported **delta 0 where +1 was asserted**. The inserted bullet file had no trailing
newline, so `cat` fused it with the line below and **Lane B's `M34` status bullet vanished into the tail of
Lane A's**. The standing *"assert a line-count delta on every `PROGRESS.md` edit"* rule caught it on the
first try, and the restore touched **only** `PROGRESS.md` — never the two doc files carrying uncommitted
work, per M9's rule that `git checkout --` is not a restore mechanism.

`lane-a.md` and every Lane A hand-off since M29 stated *"ADR-0016's next free sub-decision is `§D36` — M29
spent `§D35`."* **M29 spent no `§D` at all.** Verified here rather than accepted: `docs/adr/0016-saml-sso.md`

⚠️ **The direction it travelled is the transferable part.** Lane B may not edit `lane-a.md`, so it could only
write the correction into its own file and rely on the next Lane A session reading it. **It did, because
Rule 7 makes reading the whole of the other lane's file mandatory** — the same discipline that prevents
number collisions is what carried a correction across a boundary neither lane may write through. **A

### 2026-08-28 — M40 (Lane A): the tracker is gated, and a vacuous success was found inside the gate — PR #230, `9c20924`, 6/6 green

`scripts/tracker-lint.php` as its own CI step with `fetch-depth: 2`: seven rule groups over

constitution count, no `Current Status` in the archive, encoding, hand-off markers, and an

registered rather than merely written. It is a CI step and not a local check because the incident it
exists for **merged green** — nothing in CI had ever read a documentation diff.

⛔⛔ **`R7`, THE ONE RULE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE 1,086-LINE DELETION, WAS PERMANENTLY BLIND ON THIS
HOST AND REPORTED SUCCESS.** It used `HEAD` followed by a caret. PHP's `exec()` runs through cmd.exe on
Windows, where **the caret is the escape character**, so git received plain `HEAD`: measured, `HEAD` and
`HEAD`-caret both resolved to `216ea25` while `HEAD~1` gave `f537bea`. The rule compared the file
**against itself** and printed `+0` forever, and `rev-parse --verify` still SUCCEEDED so the
cannot-measure guard never fired. **It did not skip loudly; it passed quietly** — green on Linux CI and
blind on every local run, which is the worse half.

✅ **Found only because one control COMMITTED its mutation rather than leaving it in the working tree.**
The first harness mutated in place and `R7` reported CAUGHT — correctly, but for the wrong reason:
uncommitted, `HEAD` still held the unmutated file. ⚠️ **A control that does not reproduce CI's actual
condition can confirm a broken check as confidently as a working one.**

**Proven on both sides.** 8/8 host violations caught, both files restored byte-identically by sha256.
The declared-surgery escape proven with the mutation **committed**, because the surgery cannot merge
without it. And **the PR was deliberately red before green**: `R7`'s CI behaviour depends on
`fetch-depth: 2` and cannot be tested on the host, so a 300-line violation was pushed on purpose,
failed at step 12 naming the drop and `f565ac9`, and was reverted byte-identically in the same PR.

⚠️ **Two prescribed remedies did not work.** Asserting one `Next Session` across both tracker files
would have been RED ON ARRIVAL — the heading is byte-identical in both, so the count is 2; the gate
pins 2 and the surgery lowers it to 1. And `mutate.php` cannot prove a standalone CLI gate: it runs
Pest inside the app container.

⛔ **Six misattributions corrected.** The deletion is **J4b1's, 2026-08-16, `f565ac9`** — settled from
`git show --numstat`, not from prose. Four sites said `M31`, two said `M16`; every number was invented
by a later retelling and **M38/M39 wrote three of them**. The only site that never named an increment
is the only one that stayed true. Unlike M38's `0021` bullets, which recorded what was true when
written, this was never true at any point.

⚠️ **The absence-read-as-success family gained two members in one increment:** `HEAD`-caret comparing a
file to itself, and a watcher script reading an **empty check rollup** as *"all checks complete"*
because the previous run had just been cancelled. With `steps: []` and the path-filtered run, that is
four shapes of one defect — **absence mistaken for a passing result** — two of them found while
building the gate that exists for exactly that class. Namespaces spent: nothing, sixteenth consecutive.

So: on a **throw**, restore the PHP mirror only (the database has already reverted itself); on a **nested** success re-issue the GUC, because a `SET LOCAL` inside a savepoint **survives its release** and would otherwise hand the rest of the enclosing transaction a tenant it never asked for (the H12a sweep is exactly that); on an **outermost** success the COMMIT has already discarded it, so the mirror is all that is left. Rejected in writing: *assert the precondition and throw* (a loud total outage is still a total outage, and the `ShouldQueue` landmine survives) and *skip the wrapper when the mirror already matches* (the mirror is not a sound proxy for the GUC — that divergence is what `ScopeTenantContextToJob` exists to contain).

The palette now mints the input's id and passes `initialFocus` as a selector for it. **The general rule: an attribute that worked because a component had no wrapper is a dependency on that component's SHAPE, and wrapping is not a refactor-safe operation for it.**

Fixed by rendering `MdsTextInput`, whose root IS the input, so the explicit `role="combobox"` and the four ARIA attributes still land on the real control. **Reviewing the frame, not only measuring it, is the only thing that could have found this.**

  ⚠️⚠️ **THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND A LIVE SECURITY DEFECT AFTER ALL SIX JOBS WERE GREEN — THIRD INCREMENT RUNNING, AND THE MOST SERIOUS YET.** Four independent lenses, every finding handed to a skeptic prompted to REFUTE it: **8 raised, 3 refuted, 5 real**, two of them confirmed by the verifier *running* the mutation rather than reading. (1) **OAuth LOGIN-CSRF: nothing bound the browser that STARTED a sign-in to the one that FINISHED it.** A signed `state` proves *we* minted the token; it says nothing about who holds it. An attacker could obtain an authorization `code` without spending it, send a victim the callback URL, and `Auth::login()` would run **on the attacker's account in the victim's browser** — everything the victim then typed, uploaded or configured landing in an account the attacker controls. The tenant arm was the same attack against the handoff URL, accepted in *any* browser with an attacker-chosen `return_to`. Fixed with one session key (`google.flow_sid`) compared at both hops that create a session; no cross-host cookie and no token-format change are needed because each of those hops is same-host with its own mint, and it compares the flow's own `state_id` rather than merely requiring *some* value. ⚠️ **The connector flow does NOT supply this binding either** — its `uid` claim is for attribution and its callback never sees the tenant session — so this is not a protection J3c2 dropped but one the family never had; **ADR-0009 §D3's "the signed state is the CSRF control" is a claim about PROVENANCE that reads like one about ORIGIN**, and that is what made it easy to miss (RFC 6749 §10.12 asks for the missing half explicitly). (2) **The write-path trim evicted LIVE in-flight sign-ins** — ported faithfully from `SsoAuthFailureRecorder::trim()`, whose table holds finished log rows while this one holds live state, so a rank-only cap let anyone push a member's row past the cap while they sat on Google's consent screen: **unauthenticated denial of *authentication* for a whole workspace**, with the log blaming `state_replayed`. Liveness is now the outer `AND`; stated consequence, the table is capped at N *spent* rows plus whatever the limiter admits in one state TTL. (3) **Two tests were vacuous** — the seat-quota "no orphaned account" case asserted two things that were *unconditionally* false (one hidden by RLS with the GUCs cleared, one on a connection that structurally cannot see the test transaction), so deleting `provision()`'s transaction left all 32 green while every full-workspace sign-in stranded a live account; and the trim case compared two reads of the same surviving rows, a tautology that passed even with the subquery inverted to keep the OLDEST N. (4) Four documents claimed all three routes 404 when unconfigured; only the mint route consults the gate. (5) §7.1 implied `MemberJoined` parity across four doors — there are three, and the silent one is invitation acceptance.

It was the ONLY model in the tree missing the pairing; `tests/Unit/Models/TenantScopedContractTest.php` now asserts it in ~1s, mutation-verified. (b) A **self-deadlock**: `users.google_id` is UNIQUE so its UPDATE takes `FOR UPDATE`, while the `tenant_users` INSERT takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on the same `users` row for its FK — and the link runs on `pgsql_auth`, a **separate session**, so ordering it inside the transaction made the request wait on a transaction that could not commit until it returned. No error, no rollback, no timeout; two runs sat for 26 and 75 minutes before `pg_blocking_pids()` named the application's own connection. **A Pest run that HANGS rather than fails is a lock, not a slow host.** (c) A genuine PHPStan `method.notFound` in the committed seam: `fromSocialiteUser()` was typed against `Contracts\User`, which has no `getRaw()` — it compiled, ran and passed its unit tests (which build a concrete `Two\User`) while being wrong the moment anything checked.

  🔴 **THE ACS WAS REPLACING THE BROWSER'S SESSION COOKIE, SO P1c's STEP-UP HOP HAD NEVER WORKED IN A REAL BROWSER. MEASURED AGAINST A RUNNING STACK, NOT REASONED.** Inside `web`, `StartSession` finds no cookie on a cross-site POST, mints a fresh id, and `addCookieToResponse()` emits it **unconditionally** — its only guard is `! is_null(session.driver)`. `curl` against `fb-lane-b` returned `Set-Cookie: meridian-session=<a new, empty session>; path=/` plus a regenerated `XSRF-TOKEN`, host-only and same-path, so a browser **replaces** the member's real cookie and then follows our 302 carrying the empty one. A member completing a step-up therefore arrived with no session, was bounced to `/login` by `auth`, and had lost the session the step-up was being performed for; the regenerated CSRF token would have 419'd their next write. **P1e would have 404'd for everybody** — and, sharpest of all, **the outage and the security refusal share ONE observable**, a 404 at the hop, so an acceptance test would have passed either way. ⚠️ **No test in this repository could see it**: the Pest client never feeds `Set-Cookie` into the next request and `Store::loadSession()` merges onto a memoised store — **the harness models the session as a process global; a browser models it as a cookie.** Fixed by taking the ACS out of the stateful stack entirely, which is what its own docblock had claimed since P1b, and pinned by the one assertion that can see it: a response-header assertion.

Their `::int` casts stay correct either way; only the stated reason is stale. The branch **stays**, because the mapping is a property of a connection OPTION: one `options` override turns every flag in every artefact into the string `"f"`, which a destination trusting JSON types reads as **TRUTHY**. `DriverTypeMappingTest` pins the measured mapping. Measured too: **`numeric` stays a string** — the driver's doing, not the encoder's, and `1.50` vs `1.5` is one JSON number and two `numeric` values — while `json`/`jsonb` stay encoded text, which is the one coercion live today.

  ⚠️ **THE ROW COULD NOT BE BUILT AS NAMED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING — SIX-FOR-SIX ON VERIFYING A ROW AGAINST THE CODE.** "Dedicated-database tenancy" is foreclosed here by two things effort cannot move. **Identity is resolved BEFORE any tenant exists**: Fortify routes `/login` with `domain => null`, and `pgsql_auth` exists precisely because the join-shape RLS on `users` fails closed pre-context — so at the moment of login there is no subdomain and therefore no tenant database to look a person up in. And **three RLS policies subquery a neighbouring table** (`users`→`tenant_users`, `resource_grants`→`forms`/`scope_nodes`, draft-children→`form_versions`), which PostgreSQL cannot express across databases; a policy whose referent is absent does not fail closed, it ERRORS on every SELECT. Production is also one box with one PostgreSQL instance (ADR-0005), so the word would have bought blast-radius containment and not isolation, and **not residency at all** — which is a hosting decision, not a schema one. ADR-0017 decides isolation TIERING with the default unchanged, names **schema-per-tenant in the same instance** as the target, and records that this is not one uncommented line: stock `PostgreSQLSchemaManager` REPLACES `search_path` rather than prepending, dropping `public` and with it the `geometry` type, `users`, `tenants`, `jobs` and the `migrations` table.

  ⚠️⚠️ **THE PRODUCT HAD BEEN TELLING OPERATORS DEDICATED-DB WAS LIVE, AND NO GREP COULD HAVE FOUND IT.** `TenantDetailPresenter::features()` GENERATES its table by iterating `plans.feature_flags` and labelling unknowns with `ucfirst(str_replace('_',' ',$key))`. `EntitlementService::feature('dedicated_db')` resolves TRUE on Enterprise and `ToggleableModules` does not list it, so for every Enterprise tenant the console rendered **`Dedicated db | Plan grants: Yes | In effect: Yes | Note: —`** beside capabilities that genuinely work. Because the rows are generated, the search a reader runs before concluding "nothing consumes this key yet" — `grep dedicated_db` — returns a seeder, a docblock and one negative unit test, and never this surface. `PlanCatalog` compounded it: Enterprise's **seeded, rendered** description read *"SSO, dedicated tenancy, and data residency."* Both corrected and pinned. **This is the P1c "a test pins copy, not truth" lesson recurring one increment later, in a place a test could not have been written because nobody knew the sentence existed.**

  ⚠️ **THE SECOND DEFECT THE GUARDS FOUND: `Tenant` HAS BEEN SERVING A STALE `updated_at` SINCE THE MODEL WAS WRITTEN.** `created_at`/`updated_at` were missing from `getCustomColumns()`, so VirtualColumn's `encodeAttributes()` copied them into the `data` blob on every save and `decodeVirtualColumn()` set them back OVER the real column on every read. Eloquent stamps `updated_at` AFTER the `saving` event that does the encoding, so the copy is always one save behind — measured on the dev database: column `19:54:38`, blob `19:54:11`. `created_at` escaped notice for a year only because it never changes, so its two copies always agreed. **The whitelist alone does not heal an existing row** (the decode loop iterates the keys PRESENT IN `data`, not the non-whitelisted ones), hence migration `2026_08_16_000001`, cast through `jsonb` because the column is `json` and `-` exists only for `jsonb`.

  ⚠️ **`domains` CARRIES `tenant_id NOT NULL` AND HAS ZERO RLS POLICIES.** Correct and deliberate — it is the table read to decide WHICH TENANT a request is, so scoping it by tenant is circular — and it is exactly the case `scripts/migration-lint.php`'s own `EXEMPT_TABLES` comment denied existed ("None of these declare a bare `tenant_id`"). The consequence is why `TenantScopedTables` exists as data rather than as a rule: **any future code reasoning "carries `tenant_id`, therefore RLS is filtering it" reads every tenant's hostnames, custom domains and verification tokens.** Classification is a DECISION (`domains` is unprotected because somebody reasoned about it) and no query separates that from somebody forgetting — so the list holds the reasoning and the drift test holds the drift, in BOTH directions.

  still not reportable, but now for a KNOWN reason rather than an open one. **(3)** `find` and `glob` are
  unaffected, so any script needing a complete file list should use one of those.

  **⚠️ NO COLLISION PROBE — THE RETRY IS AT THE TRANSACTION BOUNDARY, AND THE FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG.**
  The obvious shape is `FormSlug::suggest()`'s "mint, SELECT, re-mint if taken". It cannot work here, for a
  reason `FormSlug` never faces: both writers create INSIDE `DB::transaction`, so a probe is a TOCTOU read
  that proves nothing about a concurrent inserter, and by the time the index raises 23505 the transaction is
  in ERROR state — re-minting in place is impossible (25P02). A probe's attempts are probes, not inserts.
  `SubmissionPipeline` and `SubmissionDraftService` now retry the whole closure, where a fresh
  `Submission::create()` mints again. The 23505 arms are **ORDERED rather than told apart by constraint
  name** (resolve the client-uuid race first; only an unexplained 23505 is a reference collision), which
  keeps `SavedReportViewService`'s "catch the CODE, never match the driver's message" rule intact.
  ⚠️ The backfill hit the SAME 25P02 wall in its own effect test — correct in production (autocommit),
  broken under any caller holding a transaction — so its chunk UPDATE is wrapped in a nested transaction,
  i.e. a SAVEPOINT.

  **⚠️ THE UNIQUE INDEX IS CREATED BEFORE THE BACKFILL, NOT AFTER.** Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so
  un-backfilled rows coexist under it and the backfill writes THROUGH the constraint — the database is the
  only authority. The rejected alternative (de-duplicate in a PHP `seen` set, then add the index) puts a
  second authority beside the index and can only be tested PROBABILISTICALLY. **No `deleted_at IS NULL`
  arm**, deliberately: a soft-deleted submission keeps its code reserved forever, because freeing it would
  let a code a respondent wrote down resolve LATER to a different submission — strictly worse than "not
  found". The consequence is recorded in `ReapTenantDraftsJob`, whose `forceDelete()` now frees one too.
  Verified against the real seeded database: **521 pre-existing rows, all 521 backfilled, all distinct**,
  with a clean `up → down → up` round trip.

  **⚠️ THE PREFIX SEARCH ARM IS DELETED, AND AN 8-CHARACTER ID FRAGMENT NOW MATCHES NOTHING.** That is the
  point rather than a regression: under uuidv7 those characters are a millisecond timestamp's top 32 bits,
  identical across a ~49-day window. `MIN_UUID_PREFIX` is gone; `referenceCandidate()` (exact) and
  `submissionId()` (exact, **strictly canonical**) replace it. ⚠️ The strictness is load-bearing — binding a
  non-uuid to `id = ?` raises 22P02, i.e. a 500 on an Inertia GET, where the old `id::text LIKE` merely
  matched nothing. **The two parsers are disjoint by LENGTH, never by alphabet**: hex is a strict SUBSET of
  Crockford Base32, so every 8-char hex string is also a valid reference and no alphabet test could tell them
  apart (8 vs 36 vs a de-hyphenated 32 can).

  **⚠️ ONE REFERENCE, SERVER-ISSUED — AND THE GUEST RUNTIME'S OWN CODE WAS A LIVE DEFECT NOBODY HAD FILED.**
  `deriveReference()` printed `MER-XXXXXX` on the confirmation screen and in the offline outbox, derived from
  a uuid and **stored nowhere**, so a respondent quoting it to the tenant got nothing back. The online path
  now prints the real handle; the offline one keeps its local code **relabelled as a queue tag**, with copy
  saying a reference is issued once the response is sent. `outbox-status.ts`'s rule forbidding a code change
  was right under its premise, and the premise is gone — nothing now tells the respondent the tag is their
  reference. `docs/ux/form-filling-ux-flow.md` carried the derived-reference decision in TWO places (§9 and
  numbered decision 15); both are struck rather than silently contradicted.

  **The inbox's Reference column is also its first text link to a submission.** Measured: the only way in was

Extracted to `tests/e2e/support/navigate.ts`, net −10 lines. ⚠️ **And do not write the builder glob into a docblock**: two asterisks followed by a slash CLOSE the block comment, and the file then fails to parse with "Missing semicolon" pointing at an apostrophe four lines below — nowhere near the cause, the same family as the bare tag literal that once broke the Storybook build alone.

  **⚠️ J2b's VUE HALF ALMOST SHIPPED THE DEFECT THE WHOLE ROW EXISTS TO REMOVE, AND A TEST — NOT A REVIEW — IS WHAT CLOSED IT.** `FormHubPresenter::tabs()` emitted `/forms/{form}/submissions` for the Responses tab: **that route is J2c's and does not exist**, so the hub's primary navigation would have 404'd on the page opened to kill dead ends. It now points at `/submissions?form_id={id}`, which is safe by measurement rather than by hope — `SubmissionInboxController:39` reads `form_id` as a plain query string with **no `Rule::in`** and the presenter composes it as a bare `where`, so a form with zero responses filters to an empty list instead of 422-ing on the submissions-derived dropdown. **The general fix is `FormTabSetReachabilityTest`**: a `->with()` dataset that issues a REAL request per tab href and requires a success, so no future tab can ship as a dead link. One HTTP request per case, never a loop — the tenant GUC is torn down on the way out (`FormHubGateTest` records it). J2c swaps that one line and the hub's Responses tile follows automatically, because the tile reads its href back off the tab set rather than rebuilding the URL.

  **The J1e recon, kept below as the record of what the increment was planned against.** ⚠️ **THIS IS NOT "ADD `q` SIX TIMES" - THREE OF THE SIX LISTS HAVE NO FILTER INFRASTRUCTURE AT ALL.** Measured, per presenter:

  | List | Method | Has filters? | Filter bar | `empty_reason`? |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | forms | `FormPresenter::list(User)` :27 | **NO** | **none at all** | **NO** |
  | webhooks | `WebhookEndpointPresenter::index(User)` :43 | **NO** | — | — |
  | members | `TenantMembershipService::listMembers(Tenant)` :469 | **NO** | — | — |
  | submissions | `SubmissionInboxPresenter::list(User, array $filters)` :53 | yes | Style A | — |
  | feedback | `FeedbackPresenter::index(array $filters)` :39 | yes | Style B :110 | yes |
  | audit | `AuditLogPresenter::index(User, array $filters)` :50 | yes (`AuditLogFilterRequest`) | Style B :166 | yes |

  So J1e = build a filter surface from scratch on THREE pages + add `q` to three + the audit narrowing + the `LibraryPicker` migration + tests and docs across all of it. Budget it accordingly; a half-applied pattern across six lists cannot merge.

Synchronous, no job, no storage — unlike the submission PDF, which is queued precisely because it STORES an artifact against the tenant's quota. **UNGATED by plan on purpose:** the obvious-looking `feature:ocr_single` is Professional+, and printing a blank form is useful with no OCR anywhere in the picture. **A DRAFT 404s** — not a policy preference: a draft's `schema_snapshot` is literally `[]`, so without the guard the request 200s with a titled document containing NO QUESTIONS, failing as "an empty form" rather than "a refused one". **A SUPERSEDED version still prints**, which is the case the OCR chain needs: paper already in the field was printed against the layout live at the time.

A presenter that renders the list as it arrives produces a shuffled form that is entirely plausible on any single example. The ordering test's fixture has its `key` order as the exact REVERSE of its `sequence` order, so a presence-only assertion cannot pass by accident.

(2) **`.runhead`'s offsets are page-CONTENT-relative**: `Positioner\Absolute::position()` places a fixed BLOCK at `containing_block + top` and `determine_absolute_containing_block()` gives a fixed frame the page box AFTER the `@page` margins — so `top` is negative on purpose, and that branch **never reads `right`**, which is why the width is explicit. Found by reading `vendor/dompdf`, not by looking at a PDF. Also: **no page numbers and no barcode are possible** — page counters go through `page_text()` (inline PHP, disabled by the §5 security contract) and any raster needs `ext-gd`, absent from the app container and all four CI jobs.

  **⚠️ THE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FOUND A REAL CORRECTNESS DEFECT THAT EVERY TEST WAS BLIND TO.** `cascading_select` was classified `Choices` on the strength of it having a `config.options` at all. **That option pool is ONE FLAT LIST SPANNING EVERY LEVEL**, each entry carrying its own `level` and `parent` (`StructuralValidationGate::assertCascadingResolves()`) — so the paper set **"Manila" beside "NCR" as a tick-box sibling: a child option offered as an alternative to its own parent**, a shape the screen control never shows because it narrows each level by the one above. Paper can narrow nothing, so it is now a **comb with one captioned run per declared level**, which is what a paper address block has always looked like. Its four flat siblings stay `Choices`. **Four more review findings, each fixed:** a **conditional SECTION printed entirely unmarked** (a `relevant_expression` lives on the section row and its member fields carry nothing, so the per-field marker structurally cannot see it); a field whose `section_key` matched no section **vanished from the paper silently** — the worst failure an instrument can have, now printed last under no heading; the renderer carried an optional `$brand` no caller passed and no test exercised (an untested branch pretending to be an API); and the "not collected on paper" marker shared `.q__note` with instructional prose, welding two different things together.

  **⚠️ AND A BLADE COMPILER TRAP WORTH KNOWING: `@endif@if` WRITTEN WITH NO SPACE BETWEEN THEM DOES NOT COMPILE.** Blade leaves the second directive in the output as LITERAL TEXT, which then fails as `syntax error, unexpected token "endif"` **in the compiled view under `storage/framework/views/`** — several frames away from the template line that caused it, with a hash for a filename. Space the directives apart.

  **Also pinned:** comb geometry is the ICR contract (14pt cells on a 15.5pt pitch, **max 30 per run derived from A4 minus margins**, because dompdf CLIPS an over-wide table rather than wrapping it); dates comb into captioned `DD MM YYYY` groups, since `03/04` is unrecoverable from the ink otherwise; `mb_substr`/`mb_strtoupper` on captions, because `substr` can halve a UTF-8 sequence and Blade's `e()` returns the EMPTY STRING on invalid UTF-8 — a silently missing caption, not an error; a choice field with no options gets a ruled box via `@forelse` rather than a labelled question with nowhere to answer it. **A form authored outside the WinAnsi repertoire (CJK, Arabic, Cyrillic, Thai) does not print correctly and fails silently** — recorded in §2.5.8; closing it needs an embedded TrueType font, which the §5 posture currently forbids.

A focus test asserted `document.activeElement?.textContent` CONTAINS "Keep it" - but the focused button unmounts, so activeElement falls back to `<body>`, whose text contains everything. And nothing tested that `SyncStatus` FORWARDS the review uuid, only that the child emits it, which is precisely where the bug was.

(2) **`git checkout -- <path>` RESTORES THE COMMITTED STATE, so it silently reverts review fixes** - it ate a whole batch of I10d's and one of I10b's. Use file backups for mutation testing, never `git checkout`.

Two runs settled it, neither of them CI. A **Pest test** (`tests/Feature/Auth/CentralHostLoginTest.php`) proved the whole server side clean in ONE run — a real `POST http://meridian.test/login` authenticates, the session carries into `/admin/settings`, the console renders once step-up is confirmed. Then the browser half was **reproduced against the LOCAL docker stack** (`E2E_BASE_URL=http://acme.localhost:8080` reproduces it exactly — use this instead of CI), where full response logging showed `POST 302 /login -> /dashboard`: **the login had been succeeding all along**, and the `/admin/settings` navigation was firing BEFORE the login XHR landed. **The login form is an Inertia XHR, so the page performs no document navigation and `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` resolves INSTANTLY against the already-idle previous load.** Fixes: visit `/admin/settings` as a guest FIRST so `redirect()->guest()` plants `url.intended` (without it Fortify targets `/dashboard`, a TENANT route whose `NotASubdomainException` handler redirects to an ABSOLUTE url an Inertia XHR cannot follow), then `waitForURL` as both sync point and session assertion. **TWO REAL DEFECTS FELL OUT.** (1) **Both seeders were promoting the super-admin over the app connection, affecting ZERO rows silently** — `users` has FORCE RLS, its SELECT policy is join-shaped and fails closed, and PostgreSQL applies SELECT policies to an UPDATE whose WHERE reads a column; a platform operator has no membership BY DESIGN, so a freshly seeded demo database had **no super-admin at all** and nothing said so. Fixed to `pgsql_privileged` **with a zero-row postcondition that throws** (the `OcrCompatibilityBackfill` precedent), conditional on the row being visible so RefreshDatabase contexts stay unaffected. The test that should have caught it asserted the IN-MEMORY model `forceFill()` had just mutated. (2) **`AdminLayout` overflows horizontally at 375px** — its first measurement at any viewport. Measured, not guessed: `.admin__nav` runs to 385 against 375, identically on both pages, which is the tell that it is the shell.

Every other event type has both. A tenant could tick "Submission answers edited" on `/webhooks`, point it at a SIEM, and receive nothing forever with no error — verbatim the defect the catalog's own docblock says "must not be introduced by the back door". **`WebhookFanOutTest` now asserts a dispatch listener exists for EVERY `DomainEventType` case**, so the next one cannot repeat it. **(2) `openapi.json` was not regenerated** — four `event_types` enums shipped advertising seven values while eight FormRequests accepted eight; the `DomainEventType` docblock edited in that very diff lists "a regenerated `openapi.json`" as step 4. Fixed, plus a contract test comparing the spec's enum to `DomainEventType::values()` (mutation-checked: removing one value reddens it). **(3) `AttachmentReferenceValidator` would have rejected EVERY edit of any submission with media** — it asserts `attachable_type === 'form_field'`, but `SubmissionFinalizer` re-points attachments to `'submission'` at submit. A test with a real media answer is the only reason that is not shipping.

The cause was a real bug: the service **stored `$normalized` (un-pruned) while projecting `$final` (pruned)**, so after every edit the JSONB answer document and the typed index disagreed, and an answer the original submit had pruned as irrelevant was resurrected. Both finalize doors store the pruned document; this one did not. Fixed, and the clock mutation now reddens with exactly the right message ("Failed asserting that an array has the key 'same_day_note'") — **a wrong clock silently DELETES an answer that was relevant when the response was filed.**

  **⚠️ THE LOST-UPDATE GUARD HAD TO MOVE TO THE CLIENT, AND THE FIRST VERSION WAS SECURITY THEATRE.** The write is a whole-document replace, so a second editor saving a stale page reverts everything the first corrected — silently, with an audit row diffed against the stale snapshot that says nothing about the reversion. The first attempt compared a value read at the top of `edit()` against one read under the lock, **which is always equal**, because both reads happen inside one request with nothing interleaved. The lost update spans two REQUESTS. What shipped is an optimistic-concurrency **baseline** (`answers_content_checksum`) emitted by the presenter, carried on the PATCH, and compared server-side — the same posture `routes/tenant.php` already records for the builder ("content edits carry an `updated_at` token → 409 on drift"). It also closes browser-Back-then-Save. **The rule is `present` + `nullable`, NOT `required`**: the column is nullable, so a submission stored before the pipeline stamped a checksum would otherwise be permanently uneditable.

Same hazard `SubmissionReviewService::archive()`'s `$from` refuses in writing, same answer: **a `capacity_consumed_at` column, never a fifth entry in `EDITABLE`.** The test asserts the accepted set as an EQUALITY over every `SubmissionStatus` case, so a sixth status must be classified on purpose. **Editing an APPROVED row demotes it to `under_review`** (user decision) clearing the approval stamps, as ONE combined audit row — a ledger showing "approval revoked" beside "answers edited" invites the reading that somebody revoked it deliberately. The success toast names the outcome, because `demotes_on_save` is a page-load snapshot and a reviewer can approve in another tab.

  **⚠️ PROJECTIONS WERE INSERT-ONLY AND NOTHING SAID SO.** `projectIndex`/`projectGeo` moved out of `SubmissionFinalizer` into a new `SubmissionProjectionWriter` with `write()` (finalize) and `rewrite()` (delete-then-insert, edit). **Every VALUE assertion passes against a duplicating implementation** — only a COUNT fails — so the tests assert counts. `SubmissionProjectionWriterTest` exists because the class docblock cited it and it did not: **the fourth time this project has shipped a docblock naming a guard that was never written.** It covers the geo half, which goes through raw SQL on both insert and delete.

  **⚠️ MEDIA IS READ-ONLY AND THE SERVER ENFORCES IT.** `mergeMedia()` takes media answers from the STORED document and unsets whatever the client sent — a disabled control is a suggestion when the PATCH body is plain JSON, and without the unset a hand-rolled body could re-point an arbitrary attachment onto the submission. `attachment_refs` is rewritten from `$final` through `SubmissionFinalizer::collectAttachmentIds()` (now public static), because relevance can PRUNE media even though an edit cannot add it. The media-editing half is **filed** in `docs/feature-backlog.md` with its four sub-problems and the `AttachmentReferenceValidator` warning — three comments claimed it was filed when it was not.

  **OTHER REVIEW FIXES:** `submissions.view` added as a conjunct to `update()` (here the write gate IS the read gate — a future narrow "Data Correction" role would otherwise gain a tenant-wide answer read through the one door nobody tests); `answerDiff` made key-order-insensitive (PHP `===` on arrays requires identical key ORDER, and the order of an object-valued answer is the CLIENT's, so every edit to a form with a repeat group claimed the group changed); the Edit button rewrapped as `<Link><MdsButton/></Link>` (bare `as="a"` was a full browser reload); Save rendered on every step in edit mode (it was gated behind `isLastStep`, so fixing one character on step 6 of 8 cost five pointless Next clicks); `role="alert"` → `"status"` on the edit banner (**this page's own autosave note argues it** — a live region present at first paint is not reliably announced and interrupts on the readers that do announce it); the media read-only block now renders its error (a relevance flip can make a required media field relevant, and without it the editor got "1 answer needs attention" with no message and no control); demotion copy corrected from "the review queue" to "under review" (the service sets `under_review`, so a reviewer filtering on Submitted never sees it come back). **Six stale/false doc references closed** across `webhook-integration-design.md` (the pre-specified `submission.updated` payload was wrong in three fields), `multi-tenancy-rbac-design.md`, `feature-backlog.md`, `audit-compliance-logging-spec.md`, `TESTING-GUIDE.md` (the known-gaps row said the feature was impossible; ch.6.1 is now its walkthrough) — plus "PRD Feature #12" which is the AUDIT TRAIL, used with that meaning in five other files.

I9c is that parameter's **first consumer anywhere in `app/`** since H4. A PII field inside a repeatable section redacts its SECTION key (over-redaction, never under). Only CHANGED keys are recorded — an edit row is a **diff, not a snapshot**.

Renamed. **And the full local suite needs `php -d memory_limit=3G vendor/bin/pest`** — `artisan test` re-execs and loses the flag, which is recorded in the Verification loop and cost one wasted run here anyway.

  **THE SELF-JOIN IS REAL, AND THE TRAP THAT NEARLY KILLED IT IS WORTH REMEMBERING.** Before I5 the Access toggle's "open" position could do nothing — `/register` created an account belonging to **no workspace at all**. `TenantMembershipService::joinOpenTenant()` now mints the membership at **viewer**, audited `via: self_registration`. ⚠️ **Fortify's routes carry NO tenancy middleware**, so `/register` has no tenant GUC — and under nullable_global's SELECT that makes a tenant's own rows **INVISIBLE, not absent**, so a naive read falls back to the invite-only default and "open" is unreachable **forever, failing CLOSED and silently**. `TenantSettingRegistry::forTenant()` borrows the context inside a `DB::transaction` (**`applyLocal()` is `SET LOCAL` — a no-op outside one**). `GateRegistration` refuses with **404, never 403** (a 403 confirms both that the workspace exists and that it is invite-only), and it **checks `$request->is('register')` FIRST** because `config/fortify.php`'s middleware list applies to *every* Fortify route — without that guard, closing signup would 404 `/login` for everyone.

  **⚠️ `EnforcePlatformMaintenance` IS GLOBAL AND EXEMPTS BY PATH, NEVER BY ROUTE NAME** — global middleware runs BEFORE routing, so `$request->route()` is null and a name-based list exempts NOTHING, starting with `/admin/*`: the operator would be locked out of the only page that switches maintenance off. **`EnforceTenantMaintenance` must sort AFTER identification** or there is no bound tenant, everything passes through, and the feature is **dead with a green build** — `TenancyMiddlewarePriorityTest` gained that assertion and it was **MUTATION-VERIFIED** (moving the class above `InitializeTenancyByPublicHost` reddens it). One `MaintenanceResponse` factory decides the shape once: 409 + `X-Inertia-Location` for an Inertia XHR (a bare 503 renders as Inertia's debug modal *on top of* the app), the §2.3 envelope on `/api/v1`, JSON, else the 503 blade. **Return, never `abort()`** — a throw is re-shaped by `bootstrap/app.php`'s `Throwable` fallback into `server_error`.

  **`MdsSwitch` is a real `<input type="checkbox">` with `role="switch"`, prop-for-prop identical to `MdsCheckbox`** — which is *why* the 15-control swap was mechanical, and **`NotificationPreferencesCard.test.ts` passing BYTE-UNCHANGED across it is the proof, not a coincidence**. Thumb position is the non-colour signifier (WCAG 1.4.1); DSR §3.2's "specified but NOT built" callout is rewritten with that argument per §1.2's same-PR rule. `BrandingCard`'s header was unstyled since H23a2 (scoped CSS reaches a child SFC's ROOT NODE only, and it was the one card missing the re-declared block) — fixed.
