Gate `native_connectors` Starter+, INHERITED — no new gate, no new ability, no new `UsageMetric`, no new `QueueName`. **FOUR DECISIONS LOCKED WITH THE USER UP FRONT:** (1) a row carries **MAPPED ANSWERS**, not the metadata envelope; (2) scopes are **per-file, never all-Drive**; (3) **pre-flight refresh + corrected classification**; (4) drift **pauses the rule and notifies the owner**. **THE SHARED ENGINE IS `App\Support\Mapping\*`** — `ColumnFingerprint` / `ColumnMapping` / `MappedColumn` / `MappingDrift` / `MappingDriftDetector`, pure (no HTTP, no Eloquent, no container) and pinned by `MappingNamespaceBoundaryTest`, which PARSES the namespace's own source and fails if it imports from Connectors/Ocr/Database/Http. **BOTH DIRECTIONS SHIP NOW** — `project()` writes (H16a) and `interpret()` reads (H19a's linelist) — so the reuse is demonstrable rather than asserted; a one-directional engine is exactly how H19a would have discovered the shape did not fit and written a second one. **ORDER IS PART OF THE FINGERPRINT** because both consumers address columns positionally; a set-based digest would call a reordered sheet identical and put every answer under the wrong heading, which is the failure `ocr-pipeline-design.md:84` names. **VERIFICATION NARROWED A LOCKED DECISION, IN THE DIRECTION THE USER CHOSE:** the plan said add `spreadsheets` only if required — Google's own scope table classifies `drive.file` **Recommended, Non-sensitive** for the Sheets API and `spreadsheets` **Sensitive**, so `drive.file` ships ALONE, avoiding both the wider grant and Google's sensitive-scope verification tier. **THE SHARPEST FACT IN THE INCREMENT: Google answers HTTP 401 `authError` for an EXPIRED access token and a REVOKED grant alike.** Only the token endpoint distinguishes them (`invalid_grant`), so the adapter classifies 401 as **retryable**; the obvious mapping would have revoked a live connection roughly once an hour, clearing both tokens and emailing the owner each time. **FOUR NET-NEW FRAMEWORK CHANGES, each because the alternative was wrong:** a **fourth `ConnectorDeliveryResult` outcome `blocked`** (destination unusable, credential healthy → pause ONE rule; `failed` would retry a human-only fix and `credentialRejected` would revoke a good grant over one added column); **`ConnectionTokenRefresher::ensureFresh()`** (ADR-0009 §D6's own revisit trigger, fired — Google's ~1h tokens vs an hourly sweep — as a 120s GUARD on top of the sweep, not a second policy); a **`$terminal` flag on `ConnectorOAuthException`** (the refresher marked a grant permanently dead on ANY exception **including a transport timeout** — unreachable in H15a because Slack tokens never expire, reachable on every Google send from here, and found because PHPStan reported the adapter's CREDENTIAL_ERRORS constant as unused); and **`SubscriptionConfigRules`**, because H15a's four request classes hard-coded Slack's `config.channel_id` in the shared layer, so a Sheets rule was rejected by validation before any adapter saw it. **Two more Slack-shaped seams in provider-agnostic code fixed:** `ConnectorChannelDirectory::message()` said "Slack" in every string, and `ConnectionPresenter::providerDescription()` is a `default`-less `match` that would have thrown `UnhandledMatchError` on the Integrations page. **`valueInputOption=RAW` IS A SECURITY CONTROL, not formatting:** `security-threat-model.md:127`'s formula-injection row in a worse form — a live Sheet evaluates `=IMPORTXML(...)` on GOOGLE'S servers with no human opening anything — and RAW is structural where the CSV path still owes a `'` prefix (that row stays OPEN). `insertDataOption=INSERT_ROWS` because the API DEFAULTS to OVERWRITE, which would destroy whatever the tenant keeps below their table. **`SubmissionRowProjector` EXTRACTED from `SubmissionExporter`** so a synced row and a downloaded row cannot disagree — the seam is a `fieldKey ⇒ value` MAP, not a positional row, because the two consumers order columns differently and neither ordering is more correct. **13 MUTATIONS RUN; ONE CAME BACK GREEN AND INDICTED THE CODE:** the `! $alreadyPaused` edge-trigger was unreachable (the job's own Active-status guard already stops every queued delivery behind the first block), so the flag and its comment are GONE and the test now drives TWO deliveries to pin the real mechanism. **TWO PROCESS LESSONS, both about mutations that lie.** A `sed` whose pattern never matched (`\x1E` in a BRE reduces to `x1E`) and a mutation that introduced a SYNTAX ERROR both reported "green"/"red" for reasons unrelated to the code — **verify a mutation actually applied, and `php -l` it, before believing either colour**. A third mutation was behaviourally EQUIVALENT (`$valuesByFieldKey[null]` coerces to `['']`), which looked like a test gap and was not. **Also: `git checkout --` after a mutation reverts to the COMMITTED state, silently undoing uncommitted work in the same file.** **TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY RE-READING THE ADAPTER AFTER THE SUITE WAS ALREADY GREEN, not by a failing test:** (1) **a sheet name went into A1 notation UNQUOTED** — and Google's own default tab for a form-linked sheet is `Form Responses 1`, with spaces, so `Form Responses 1!1:1` is unparseable and an entirely ordinary destination would have failed; worse, it fails as a **400**, which the classifier treated as transient, so it would have burned the whole seven-day ladder and dead-lettered with the tenant never told why. Quoting is now unconditional, with an internal apostrophe DOUBLED per A1's own rule. (2) **a 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is also Google's answer for a TAB THAT NO LONGER EXISTS** — the likeliest way a working rule breaks after setup — so it is now `blocked` rather than retried. Both are pinned (reverting the quoting reddens 2, reverting the 400 arm reddens 1). **AND THE `git checkout --` TRAP BIT A THIRD TIME IN ONE SESSION**, discarding both of these while they were still uncommitted and making one mutation run measure unfixed code — **commit BEFORE mutating, every time**. **KNOWN NARROWINGS, recorded not discovered later:** no identity scope ⇒ `external_account_id` is a constant ⇒ **one live Google connection per tenant** (a second replaces the first); **no `channel_lister`** (per-file access cannot enumerate — the picker is H16b's client-side Google Picker); **event-driven append only** (scheduled sync + historical backfill are named out of scope); and the exported `openapi.json` shows every destination key as optional, because which are required depends on the connection's provider — **and that contract nearly regressed silently**: Scramble reads `rules()` statically, so returning the whole shape from a method degraded `config` to an array-of-strings, which the CI gate could NOT catch because it only diffs a fresh export against the committed file and both were equally wrong. Fixed with a static `documentedShape()` union plus dynamic `requiredFor()`. **Docs: ADR-0009 §D6 + §D8 amended in place with the reasoning (both revisit triggers fired) and its "When to Revisit" first bullet answered; `data-privacy-gdpr-compliance.md` §7 revised IN THIS INCREMENT as that bullet itself demanded — the connector envelope is no longer metadata-by-default, and the erasure asymmetry (a row already in the tenant's Drive cannot be recalled) is recorded; `webhook-integration-design.md` §4 row 4 built-note; threat-model addendum; data-dictionary §25 `config` shape.**

- **H25 (as-built, MERGED PR #93 `c2e0223`, 6/6 CI green on the FIRST run — Contract 48s, frontend 1m15s, static 1m41s, a11y 2m11s, Pest 3m53s, E2E 11m17s) — the R5 published-version immutability guard, and the schema's FIRST database trigger.** Ships **ADR-0013 in-PR** (the H22a/ADR-0012 precedent). **R5 had been open since the architecture doc was written** and was one of only two rows in the §9 register still marked *Still OPEN*; it lost its forcing moment when the 2026-07-21 decision chose relevance-derived step-skipping over a stored step graph, and became this hardening PR. **THE GAP, PRECISELY:** a published version's CONTENT has been frozen in Postgres since Increment D (`draftChildGuard` gates every child write behind `EXISTS (fv.status = 'draft')`), but its OWN ROW was not — `formVersionGuard` leaves UPDATE deliberately status-blind so publish can flip draft→published→superseded, so `schema_snapshot`, `checksum`, `version_number`, `title`, `published_at` were all freely rewritable on a live published row, **and `status` could be set back to `'draft'`, which RE-OPENS every child row, because the child guard keys on exactly that value**. **RLS structurally cannot close it and this is not a preference:** a policy sees only OLD in `USING` and only NEW in `WITH CHECK`, and no clause can compare them, while a per-column immutability rule IS that comparison; a CHECK cannot see OLD either. **AS BUILT:** `form_versions_published_immutable_trg`, `BEFORE UPDATE … FOR EACH ROW`, gated `WHEN (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'draft')` — the gate keys on `OLD.status` and NEVER on `published_at`, because `ConnectorFanOutTest:146` legitimately writes `published_at` onto a draft row, and it lives in the `WHEN` clause and nowhere else (two copies drift, and the drift direction where WHEN fires but the body early-returns is fail-open — plus `pg_get_triggerdef()` then carries the predicate, which is what the structural test pins). **(1) DENY BY DEFAULT is the whole design** — there is NO list of frozen columns, because a hand-list is fail-OPEN for the future (a column added later would be silently mutable and nothing in CI would notice: `scripts/migration-lint.php` early-returns on alter-only migrations, so this migration's own green is VACUOUS and the three test files are the only things standing over the guard). It diffs the WHOLE ROW, `to_jsonb(OLD)` vs `to_jsonb(NEW)` per key, against a four-name allowlist — a feature test adds a column inside the test transaction and proves it is already frozen. **(2) Compared as `::text`, not as jsonb** — jsonb equality is numeric-aware (`'1'::jsonb = '1.0'::jsonb` is TRUE), so a scale-only rewrite would pass a jsonb `=` guard while silently invalidating `checksum`, which is SHA-256 over the canonical TEXT and is the offline-sync cache-buster; `::text` still treats a key-reordered snapshot as unchanged (jsonb normalises key order at parse time), and both halves are tested. The projection is also NULL-safe by construction (a SQL NULL becomes the jsonb value `null`), which matters because SEVEN frozen columns are nullable — including `created_at`, since `timestampsTz()` emits both timestamps nullable — and the suite routinely makes published rows with a NULL `checksum`; **no bare `<>` appears anywhere and a unit test asserts that absence**. **(3) FOUR INDEPENDENT RULES, not chained** (a bare `updated_at` touch on a superseded row must pass, or the guard is stricter than the invariant): frozen columns; `status` may only move `published → superseded`, `superseded` terminal, **never back to draft**; `superseded_at` writable only by that flip and only out of NULL; and **`published_by` may be CLEARED but never re-pointed**. **THAT FOURTH RULE IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THIS BROKEN and it is not obvious:** `published_by` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` against `users`, and PostgreSQL runs that referential action as an ordinary UPDATE through SPI — **it bypasses RLS but NOT a trigger** — so freezing the column outright would have made user hard-deletion (and GDPR erasure with it) permanently impossible, raising a form-version error from an unrelated tenant's row on a statement about `users`. A feature test hard-deletes a publisher and asserts the version survives with a null attribution (the publisher must be a distinct user from the form owner — `forms.owner_user_id` is `ON DELETE NO ACTION` — and an active member, because `users` carries a join-shape SELECT policy and Postgres applies SELECT policies to a WHERE-qualified DELETE, so a non-member would match zero rows and the test would pass vacuously). **(4) Refusals raise SQLSTATE 23001** (`restrict_violation`) naming every offending column (`string_agg`, alphabetical), the row id and the status — unambiguous here because Postgres core never emits it (a RESTRICT FK raises 23503) and nothing else in the codebase does, which is also what proves the TRIGGER refused a write and not the policy (an RLS `WITH CHECK` failure is 42501, and BEFORE ROW triggers run first). **Deliberately NO renderer in `bootstrap/app.php`:** reaching this guard means a code path bypassing the service layer, and a loud 500 is correct — mapping it to a friendly error would normalise exactly what R5 exists to surface. **SCOPE IS UPDATE ONLY, AND THE RESIDUAL IS NEW RISK R12** (user decision, taken before building): a `BEFORE DELETE` row trigger fires on FK cascades too, so it would turn tenant hard-delete and form hard-delete into an error, and would break `SavedReportViewWebTest:239`. So a `forms`/`tenants` hard-delete still wipes published versions through the cascade (referential actions bypass RLS) and `TRUNCATE` bypasses row triggers entirely — recorded as **R12** with a revisit trigger (the first production hard-delete path) rather than silently inherited. **The guarantee is worded "a published version cannot be EDITED", never "cannot be destroyed", everywhere it appears.** **A COMPANION `form_versions_status_chk` SHIPS IN THE SAME MIGRATION and is not scope creep** — `status` was a bare `varchar(20)` with no CHECK, and the trigger TURNS THAT INTO A TRAP by treating anything that is not `'draft'` as frozen, so one typo'd status would freeze a row permanently in a state no code can read. **`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` IS MANDATORY, NOT STYLISTIC, AND CI CANNOT CATCH IT:** `db:wipe` drops tables/views/types and NEVER routines, so `DROP TABLE … CASCADE` takes the trigger while the function survives — a bare `CREATE FUNCTION` dies on the SECOND `migrate:fresh` on any database, which every CI job avoids by provisioning a fresh one, so it would ship green and break only developers. Verified by running `migrate:fresh` twice. `down()` drops trigger-then-function (the trigger DEPENDS on the function) and never `CASCADE`s. **NAMING — this PR names the convention**, since the repo had zero triggers, trigger functions, `DB::unprepared` or `plpgsql` anywhere: **`_trg` for a trigger, `_fn` for its function, same base name, the table prefixing the function** (function names are schema-global, trigger names are per-table), all under the 63-byte `NAMEDATALEN` that truncates SILENTLY. **THREAT MODEL, STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN OVERCLAIMED:** `meridian_app` OWNS the table, so it can `ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER`; a superuser can `SET session_replication_role = 'replica'`. That is the asymmetry with RLS, where `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` was chosen *precisely because* it binds the owner — so this is an **integrity guard against application bugs and raw queries** (R5's own wording is "accidentally mutates"), **not a security boundary**. What it DOES add over RLS: it binds `pgsql_privileged` (a real superuser bypasses RLS and never a trigger — its own test pack, which needs a COMMITTED fixture on that connection or it passes vacuously, since RefreshDatabase wraps only the default one), and it fires on referential actions. **No GUC hatch** (a custom `app.*` GUC is settable by any role, so it would be no obstacle to the threat); the break-glass is written down instead — `DISABLE TRIGGER` … `ENABLE TRIGGER` inside its own migration, loud and reviewable. Trigger left in origin mode (`tgenabled = 'O'`), not `ENABLE ALWAYS`, which would fire during logical-replication apply and break a future replica restore replaying a supersede. **ONE LIVE DEFECT CLOSED IN PASSING, and it was the one reachable production path into this hole:** `FormService::updateMetadata()` wrote `title`/`description` to `whereKey($form->draft_version_id)` from an IN-MEMORY `$form`, with no lock and no re-read — so if that model was loaded before a concurrent publish, an ordinary form-settings save silently rewrote a PUBLISHED version's title, which is literally the R5 bug; now predicated on `status = 'draft'` so the stale write degrades to a no-op. **ONE DRIFTED FACT CORRECTED:** `FormBuilderService::rowVersion()`'s docblock claimed microsecond precision — Laravel's `Schema\Builder::$defaultTimePrecision` is 0 and the repo never overrides it, so the column is `timestamp(0)`; the real consequence (two builder edits inside one second are an undetectable lost update) is RECORDED, not fixed here, because it is not R5. **DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED, recorded rather than built:** `draft → superseded` directly (the trigger is silent on draft rows by construction, and firing on them is what the operation-scoping forbids); it is a lifecycle bug, not an immutability breach, because nothing was ever published. **Docs: ADR-0013 + reconciliations to seven siblings** — `form-versioning-schema-migration.md` (**v1.1**, new §2.1: §2's "RLS, not a trigger" resolution STANDS for the three child tables and is narrowed to them, with the boundary stated once — *row-scoped ⇒ RLS, OLD-vs-NEW ⇒ trigger, one member today*), `architecture/technical-architecture.md` (R5 → **RESOLVED**, **new R12**, §6.2 point 4's note amended where it asserted "one single DB-level-guard idiom", Appendix A item 5 closed — and promoted to an ADR exactly as that appendix's closing line anticipated), `data-dictionary.md` §3 (the file had NO mention of any immutability guard), `adr/0002` (a *narrowed, not superseded* note — it is what made "RLS is the one idiom" load-bearing), `workflow-branching-design.md` (§1 and the deferred list both pointed at H25), `testing-strategy.md` (the pack, plus the three reusable harness rules it encodes), `PRD.md` (ADR index). **Gates: Pest 2201 (+52 — 17 unit + 32 feature + 3 privileged), full suite green**; PHPStan **exactly 55**, the documented local phantom baseline, **zero introduced, verified PER FILE** (the two naming `FormBuilderService` are the pre-existing `FormField::$created_by`/`$updated_by` phantoms whose line numbers merely moved 9 down); Pint / controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint green; **no `openapi.json` change** (DDL-only cannot drift Scramble), no frontend change, golden corpora byte-untouched. The 1400s suite time is the documented host-memory-pressure artifact, not this branch.

- **H23b (as-built, MERGED PR #98 `b3a7971`, 6/6 CI GREEN ON THE FIRST RUN — Contract 50s, frontend 1m28s, static 1m35s, a11y 2m21s, Pest 3m43s, E2E 13m43s) — tenant branding reaches the PUBLIC GUEST RUNTIME, offline-cached; the branding vertical is COMPLETE and Phase 3 has no unblocked rows left.** **The E2E job is the load-bearing gate here**: it is the only one that loads the guest runtime in a real Chromium, registers the service worker, primes the caches and reloads offline — so the shared partial, the corrected `theme-color` and the `?b=` manifest link are verified against a live browser rather than only against assertions. (The local dev DB is EMPTY — 0 tenants, 0 forms — so the manual browser check in the plan was deliberately NOT done rather than seed the user's environment uninvited; CI's E2E covers the same ground.) Built off `main`, NOT off #97, exactly as row 258 scopes it (tokens + offline cache-invalidation; the logo is not in it). **THE APPLICATION HALF IS THE EASY HALF AND IT STILL HAD ONE TRAP.** The guest shell can never carry `data-theme-mode`, so a guest-specific two-block emission naming only `:root` looked obviously right and is WRONG: inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` a bare `:root` is (0,1,0) and **loses** to `theme-overrides.css`'s own system-dark block at `:root:not([data-theme-mode='light']):not([data-theme-mode='dark'])` — (0,3,0). So the emission is a **single shared Blade partial** (`resources/views/partials/brand-ramp.blade.php`) included by BOTH the admin root and the guest shell, third block and all; the `[data-theme-mode='dark']` block is inert on the guest shell and kept anyway, because two copies of that specificity reasoning is precisely the drift the ADR is a cautionary tale about. **Callers own WHETHER, the partial owns HOW**: the admin root additionally withholds the ramp when a member has expressed an accent opinion (H23a3's server-side precedence), while the guest shell has **no precedence rule at all** — a respondent has no preferences for the brand to lose to, which is ADR-0014 §D1's two-layers/two-audiences split working rather than an inconsistency to tidy. **ONE READER FOR THREE SURFACES:** `App\Services\Branding\GuestBrandingPresenter` (sibling of `BrandingPresenter`, which serves the settings card and must DISCLOSE what the engine changed — a respondent is told none of that). `TenantBrandingService::sharedRamp()` **is** usable here, unlike in H23a4: the guest group runs `InitializeTenancyByPublicHost`, so `TenantContract` is bound; a queue worker binds nothing. Still read through `isActive()` and never `hasBrandRamp()` — a downgraded tenant keeps its stored ramp and renders unbranded, pinned by its own test. **ONE LIVE DEFECT CLOSED IN PASSING, on exactly this surface, and the user approved it before building:** the shell's `<meta name="theme-color">` and `PwaManifestController::THEME_COLOR` were both hard-coded `#1B5E5E` = `--mds-accent-teal-600` since G8a — but the guest shell has NEVER emitted `data-accent`, so it paints Blueprint, and the browser chrome plus the installed app's splash screen were tinted a colour appearing **nowhere in the form**. `theme-color` now means one thing in both cases — the light `--mds-color-action-primary-bg` — tenant-derived when branded, `--mds-primary-600` (`#1C4B72`) when not. `background_color` stays `--mds-neutral-50`: §D7 keeps the tenant layer off neutrals, and the two sit adjacent in one payload, which is where that rule is easiest to break. **THE OFFLINE HALF IS THE HARD HALF, AND THE DESIGN DECISION IS "RE-PRIME, NEVER PURGE."** The brand rides the shell HTML, which the SW caches `NetworkFirst` under `guest-shell-html` — so the page in front of the respondent self-heals on any successful online load and needs no invalidation. What does not self-heal is every OTHER `/f/…` shell the device cached earlier (a second form, a resume link), stale until its 7-day expiry. **`caches.delete('guest-shell-html')` is the obvious fix and it is the wrong one**: a stale brand is COSMETIC, a purged shell costs a fieldworker offline access to a form they deliberately primed, which is a core PRD promise — a bad trade in any brand's favour. So `lib/brand-cache.ts` REFRESHES: a 12-hex fingerprint (`substr(sha256(json_encode(tokens)),0,12)`, `'none'` unbranded) rides `data-brand-version` on the mount node; after mount the SPA compares it with Dexie `app_state['brand_version']` and, when different **and online**, re-fetches every cached shell except the current URL and `cache.put`s **only on a 200** (writing a 404 over a working offline shell is strictly worse than the stale colour). **Different and OFFLINE ⇒ defer and change NOTHING, including the fingerprint** — advancing it without having refreshed anything is a lie that permanently suppresses the retry, since every later boot would compare equal and skip. That negative is the single most important behaviour in the file and has its own test. The manifest link carries the same fingerprint as `?b=` because the SW never caches that URL and the browser caches it hard; safe for app identity, since the manifest declares an explicit `id` so the URL is not what pins an installed app. `guest-schema` / `guest-shell-assets` untouched — neither carries brand. Dexie goes to **v2** for the new `app_state` store (a new STORE needs a bump; G8c's un-indexed `conflict_code` correctly did not), with a test proving the v1 outbox survives the upgrade — a bump that dropped a respondent's queued work for a cosmetic feature would be the worst possible trade here. **ONE TEST-HARNESS TRAP WORTH CARRYING, AND IT MAKES A CORRECT PRODUCT LOOK BROKEN:** the natural proof that "the fingerprint moves when the brand moves" is to re-brand mid-test and re-render — and it FAILS, because within one Pest test the container keeps the `Tenant` bound by the FIRST request (stancl `Tenancy::initialize()` early-returns when the tenant key is unchanged, `Tenancy.php:43`), so the second render reports the OLD ramp. Asserting the DERIVATION instead is both correct and stronger: the change property then follows from SHA-256 rather than from one sampled pair. **Any test mutating tenant state between two HTTP calls in one Pest test is exposed to this.** **ONE PROXY ASSERTION RETIRED, DELIBERATELY AND WITH THE PIN LEFT SHARPER:** `GuestRuntimeTest` pinned "no personalization on the guest shell" by searching the WHOLE document for `data-theme-mode` — which the shared partial now legitimately NAMES in a selector. That one axis moved to the `<html>` **open tag** (what the invariant was always about); the other three stayed whole-document, and a new case proves the root element is attribute-free **while the brand block is present**, asserted as a user with maximal preferences. **Gates: Pest 2287 (+11), full suite green; Vitest 1189 (+8, 55 files); vue-tsc BOTH tsconfigs, Vite build, Pint, controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint all clean; PHPStan exactly 55, zero introduced, VERIFIED PER FILE (none of the three touched/new PHP files appears in the breakdown). No migration, no `/api/v1` route, `openapi.json` byte-identical.** Docs: ADR-0014 as-built (the fifth consuming surface, and it CAN resolve `var()` — so §D8's revisit trigger, which asks for a SIXTH, does not fire), `offline-first-sync-design.md` **§4.1 new** (the re-prime rule + the `app_state` store), DSR §2.9 governing rule, `testing-strategy.md` (three generalising lessons). **ADR-0014's two stale Consequences paragraphs were deliberately NOT touched — PR #97 already strikes both through in place, and duplicating that here guarantees a conflict when #97 lands.**

- **H23a4 (as-built, BUILT + 6/6 CI GREEN ON THE FIRST RUN as PR #97 — Contract 45s, frontend 1m30s, static 1m55s, a11y 2m28s, Pest 4m5s, E2E 13m1s — but DELIBERATELY LEFT UNMERGED at the user's request, 2026-08-05; they want to revisit it first, so do NOT merge it unprompted) — tenant branding reaches EMAIL and the PDF, and the QUEUE is the hard part.** ADR-0014 §D8 stores the derived ramp because three of the five consuming surfaces cannot resolve a CSS custom property; until this increment that was an argument about consumers that did not exist. **THE FACT THE WHOLE INCREMENT TURNS ON, AND IT IS INVISIBLE FROM THE CALL SITE:** a queued `Notification` is delivered by the framework's `SendQueuedNotifications`, **NOT** by `TenantAwareJob` — so on the worker `TenantContext::currentTenantId()` is null, and `TenantBrandingService::isActive()` reads its entitlement half from **exactly that static, not from its `$tenant` argument**. Branding resolved inside `toMail()` therefore fails closed and sends EVERY tenant an unbranded email **with a green suite**; `sharedRamp()` is worse still, resolving a container binding no worker makes and returning null unconditionally. So **`App\Support\Branding\BrandPalette` resolves the palette where the tenant IS known and it rides the payload as a scalar array** (R3-legal) — the same discipline every `TenantUrl`-built link already follows. `BrandedMailDispatchTest` **flushes the GUC before running a real worker**, so the test fails if the payload is not already correct. `BrandPalette::forTenant()` additionally **REFUSES TO ANSWER** when its argument is not the ambient tenant, turning `isActive()`'s latent cross-tenant read — plan question for one tenant, storage question for another, no error — into defined, fail-closed behaviour. **THE MAIL LAYER IS "THE FIRST OF ALL OF THOSE", exactly as `TenantMail`'s docblock predicted in H17:** no `resources/views/mail`, no `resources/views/vendor`, no published theme. So `GET /branding/logo`, unauthenticated, on the tenant APP host (ADR-0009 §D2 scopes a custom domain to the guest runtime), **deliberately UNSIGNED** because an expiry on an image sitting in an inbox is a broken image on a timer — bounded instead by resolving `tenants.logo_attachment_id` and never an id from the path (so it is not a public read primitive over `attachments`, and removal takes effect immediately), the `isActive()` gate, the scan-status gate, `nosniff`, and H23a2's content-sniffed allowlist that keeps SVG out of storage. - **H23a3 (as-built, MERGED PR #96 `a1f4ffa`, 6/6 CI green on the FIRST run — Contract 55s, frontend 1m29s, static 1m46s, a11y 2m18s, Pest 4m16s, E2E 13m6s) — tenant branding reaches the ADMIN APP, and the precedence rule that makes "personalization wins" real.** **THE HEADLINE IS THAT H23a1's OWN DOCUMENTED FIX WAS WRONG, AND BUILDING IT IS HOW IT WAS FOUND.** DSR §395 predicted the Blueprint-escape would be closed with an explicit `data-accent="blueprint"` plus a `:root[data-accent='blueprint']` restoring rule. **That rule is (0,2,0) and the tenant ramp's light block is (0,1,0), so it would have outranked the brand in EVERY case — the tenant's colour would never have applied at all.** Not merely more complex: wrong. §395 is CORRECTED to describe what was built rather than left standing. **AS BUILT — PRECEDENCE IS RESOLVED ON THE SERVER, NOT IN CSS:** `app.blade.php` emits the tenant ramp **only when the member has expressed no accent opinion**. Picked Teal → Teal's existing `[data-accent='teal']` rules apply over the base tokens exactly as before; picked Blueprint → the base tokens, which ARE Blueprint, so **no restoring rule needs to exist**; no opinion → the tenant ramp. **Personalization cannot lose a specificity contest it never enters.** The CSS route was rejected on inspection because the ramp needs `:root` + `[data-theme-mode='dark']` + a `prefers-color-scheme` twin — (0,1,0), (0,2,0), (0,3,0) — and the user's teal rule at (0,2,0) would have **TIED** with the tenant's dark block, leaving source order to decide; **G11 already shipped that exact bug once.** **THE SEMANTIC CHANGE THAT MAKES THE ESCAPE EXPRESSIBLE:** `user_ui_preferences.accent_token` widens from `{NULL,'teal'}` to `{NULL,'blueprint','teal'}`. **NULL now means exactly one thing — "no opinion"** — and Blueprint is stored EXPLICITLY. The old mapping collapsed "never chose" and "chose the default" into one row, which is precisely what left a member of a branded tenant unable to ask for the product blue back. **No migration** — the column already permitted the wider domain. `defaultUiTheme()` returns **null** rather than `'blueprint'` for the same reason: a user who has never opened Settings has refused nothing, and `'blueprint'` would have made every un-personalized member silently opt OUT of their own organisation's branding. **READ THROUGH `TenantBrandingService::isActive()`, NEVER `hasBrandRamp()`** — stored and active are different questions and a surface that checks the wrong one ships a Starter+ feature to Free tenants with nothing in the build to notice; `sharedRamp()` is **fail-closed off-tenant** (mirroring `EntitlementService::snapshot()` on the same middleware) and ships **only the twelve tokens**, because the measurements and input hex are the settings card's business and would put ~2KB of contrast tables into every render. The blade's accent check becomes a **real whitelist**, matching the comment two lines above it that already claimed one, and emits `data-accent` **only for Teal** — so §2.9's absence-as-default convention survives at the ATTRIBUTE level unchanged. **TWO VERIFICATION LESSONS WORTH CARRYING:** (1) **a test written in this increment was passing VACUOUSLY and a SIBLING caught it** — `user_ui_preferences` is RLS-scoped to `app.current_user_id`, which the request tears down, so "stores an explicit null" was asserting `toBeNull()` against a row it could not SEE rather than against a null column; it passed for the wrong reason until the next test needed that row to still hold its other axes. Both now re-enter tenant context before reading. (2) **five existing tests failed and were SUPPOSED to** — they pin the old semantics ("stores the blueprint default as NULL", "resolves a NULL accent_token back to blueprint"); each was REWRITTEN to assert the new contract with the reasoning inline rather than having its expected value flipped, and one now also asserts that `AccentToken::fromColumn()` still performs the old collapse, since that helper survives and answers its own narrower question. **Gates: Pest 2276 (+10), full suite green; Vitest 1181; PHPStan exactly 55, zero introduced, verified PER FILE — it read 56 and the extra was mine, a stale `accent: string` annotation on `uiTheme()`; Pint / vue-tsc / controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint / `composer audit` clean. No migration, no route change, no `openapi.json` drift.**

- **H23a2 (as-built, MERGED PR #95 `c40a3de`, 6/6 CI green after ONE red cycle — see the withoutVite note at the end of this bullet) — tenant branding STORAGE plus the admin card, and the card's job is to say what the engine changed.** **STORAGE:** three `tenants` columns — `primary_color` (the hex the tenant TYPED, an INPUT not a rendered value), `brand_ramp` jsonb (the twelve derived hexes + 17 measured ratios + `engine_version`) and `logo_attachment_id` (FK → `attachments`, `nullOnDelete`). Two were spec'd in data-dictionary §114–115 long before anything built them; **`brand_ramp` is the new one and it earns its place for ADR-0014 §D8's reason — three of the five consuming surfaces cannot resolve a CSS custom property AT ALL** (mail clients strip `<style>` and ignore `var()`; dompdf supports neither custom properties nor `oklch()`), so once the ramp must exist as data, re-deriving it on read is duplication with a drift hazard attached. **THE TRAP THAT FAILS SILENTLY, and the reason `BrandingStorageTest` exists at all:** `tenants` is a stancl/tenancy model, and a real column NOT listed in `Tenant::getCustomColumns()` is relocated into the `data` json store and read back as **NULL** — no error, a green write path, and branding that simply never applies. The migration ships the three list additions in the SAME commit, and the test reads the columns back through **raw SQL** so a mis-store cannot hide behind the accessor. That matters more than usual because `migration-lint` keys on `Schema::create` and skips alter-only migrations, so **this migration's own CI green is VACUOUS** (the H25 lesson, verbatim). **ONE THING THE PLAN GOT WRONG AND A TEST CAUGHT:** the migration docblock originally credited `ON DELETE SET NULL` with stopping a deleted logo from rendering. **It does not.** `Attachment` uses `SoftDeletes`, so an ordinary `delete()` leaves the row and the referential action NEVER FIRES — the pointer goes on pointing at a trashed row. What actually saves the render path is the **SoftDeletes global scope on the relation**; the FK earns its keep only on `forceDelete()`. Both halves are asserted separately now, because either one alone teaches the wrong model. **THE GATING ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN AND MUST NOT BE TIDIED:** the two WRITES carry `feature:branding` (Starter+, already in `PlanCatalog.php:54` — not re-litigated); **the two REMOVALS deliberately do NOT.** ADR-0012 §D9 applied — a tenant that brands on Starter and downgrades to Free keeps a stored ramp, stops rendering branded, and must retain a path to DELETE what a paid tier let them create; gate the removals and they are stranded with a brand they can neither use nor remove. `BrandingRoutesTest` asserts BOTH directions, because making all four match looks like a cleanup. The same distinction is why `TenantBrandingService::isActive()` (stored AND entitled) is separate from `Tenant::hasBrandRamp()` (stored): confuse them one way and the paid feature is free, the other way and a downgraded tenant loses their own settings card. **THE SNAP DISCLOSURE IS THE POINT OF THE UI, not a nicety** — §D2 discards the tenant's lightness, so what renders is frequently NOT what they typed, and the ADR requires that be DISCLOSED rather than discovered: the card shows the submitted swatch beside the derived one, says plainly whether it was adjusted, previews BOTH themes, and prints all 17 ratios **worst-first by HEADROOM** (a 4.6:1 needing 4.5 is tighter than a 5.2:1 needing 3.0 — sorting by raw ratio would bury the number a sceptic wants). The preview runs the TS twin so the ramp is visible before saving, and both the `adjusted` rule and the ordering live in `brand-ramp.ts` rather than the component because each already has a PHP twin in `BrandingPresenter` and a third inline copy would be a third place to drift. **SVG IS REFUSED AS A LOGO AND THAT IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, not a limitation:** it is XML that can carry `<script>` and a logo is served same-origin to every respondent of every branded form — stored XSS (threat-model §6). Refused at the request rule AND by the service's CONTENT-SNIFFED allowlist, since `mimetypes:` trusts a client-controlled header. GIF is out too, for the duller reason that an animated logo on every form header is a WCAG 2.2.2 problem nobody would think to check. **The logo is the first attachment whose owner is not form-scoped**, so it stores the morph alias `tenant` — **DELIBERATELY not registered in the global morph map**, following the warning already in `AppServiceProvider` about `audits.auditable_type`: registering it would change how Sanctum's `tokenable_type` and Spatie's `model_type` serialize a Tenant and split existing rows between alias and FQCN. Nothing in this codebase resolves `->attachable`, and `BrandingMorphAliasTest` pins that the absence is deliberate. **FOUR THINGS THE LOCAL GATES CAUGHT THAT REVIEW WOULD NOT:** (1) the design system's OWN `token-references` guard rejected two token names invented in the Vue file — `--mds-color-text-muted` and `--mds-color-border-subtle` do not exist (they are `-text-secondary` / `-border-default`); (2) the role is **`form_editor`, not `editor`**, and `catalogRole()` returns an EMPTY STRING for an unknown name, which surfaces as an invalid-uuid `QueryException` rather than anything legible; (3) **`UploadedFile::fake()->image()` needs GD, which this container lacks** — it throws a LogicException rather than skipping, so the fixture uses real 1×1 PNG bytes exactly as `StorageQuotaEnforcementTest` already does, which also means `getMimeType()` content-sniffs for real; (4) **the tenant GUC is torn down after every HTTP request**, so a mid-test downgrade needs `enterTenant()` before `assignPlanTier()` or the `subscriptions` insert fails RLS with 42501. **Gates: Pest 2266 (+26), full suite green; Vitest 1181 (+4) across 54 files; Pint / vue-tsc / Vite build / controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint / `composer audit` clean. PHPStan exactly 55, zero introduced, VERIFIED PER FILE — it read 57 first and BOTH extras were mine** (an int/string user id, a `BelongsTo` missing its generics), while the `FormField` and `two_factor_secret` entries in the same output are pre-existing phantoms whose line numbers merely moved — and the new method was checked explicitly for the H24b2 docblock-orphaning trap. **No `/api/v1` route added, so no `openapi.json` drift.** **ONE RED CI CYCLE, AND THE LESSON IS REUSABLE: a Pest GET that asserts Inertia renders the ROOT VIEW, so `@vite` runs and needs a manifest — and the CI tests job NEVER builds assets.** Without `$this->withoutVite()` the three page-render tests passed LOCALLY (because `public/build/` survives from a dev build and is gitignored) and failed in CI as **"Not a valid Inertia response"**, which is really a 500 from `ViteManifestNotFoundException` wearing a misleading message. `AnalyticsPageGateTest` and `SuperAdminConsoleTest` already carried the call with that exact comment; this file did not, and these were **the first tests in the repo to GET `/settings`**. Diagnosed by deleting `public/build` locally to reproduce CI's condition exactly, then MUTATION-VERIFIED — the failure returns when the line is commented out. **Any new Pest GET that asserts Inertia needs `withoutVite()`.**

- **H23a1 (as-built, MERGED PR #94 `567742e`, 6/6 CI green on the FIRST run — Contract 45s, frontend 1m17s, static 1m39s, a11y 2m5s, Pest 4m11s, E2E 12m45s) — the tenant brand-ramp engine, and the ADR that reverses a ratified design-system rule.** Ships **ADR-0014 in-PR** (the ADR-0012/ADR-0013 precedent) because it overturns a decision rather than adding one. **WHAT UNBLOCKED IT:** the user answered the costed three-way fork on 2026-08-05 — see the Current Status headline for the three answers and the four-PR split. **THE FACT THE WHOLE INCREMENT TURNS ON, and it is not obvious until you measure: a brand hex is not a token.** Teal — the one hue the design system already lets a USER choose — needed **six tokens per theme** (fill / hover / active / fg / tint / ring) and carries **seventeen measured pairings** in DSR §4.1. So "validate the tenant's colour" describes nothing that can be done: there is nothing to validate until eleven other colours exist, and it is those eleven that decide legibility. The increment therefore ships a **generator**, not a validator. **AS BUILT:** `ColorSpace` (sRGB ⇄ OKLCh + WCAG contrast), `BrandRamp` (the 12-hex value object), `BrandRampGenerator`, `BrandRampException`, a TypeScript twin at `packages/design-system/src/theme/brand-ramp.ts`, and `tests/fixtures/brand-ramp.json`. It holds the tenant's **hue**, caps **chroma** at 0.11 (≈1.3× the most saturated ratified accent — Blueprint measures 0.0832, Teal 0.0651), **discards lightness entirely** and re-derives it per role by sweeping against a fixed ground until all seventeen pairings measure clean. **Lightness is discarded because lightness IS contrast** — keeping the tenant's L would keep the one property that decides whether white button text is legible; the consequence, which H23a2's UI must DISCLOSE rather than let a tenant discover, is that `#FF0000` and `#8B0000` give near-identical ramps and every achromatic input gives the SAME grey ramp (three corpus vectors pin it). **WHY IT CAN ALWAYS SUCCEED — this is what makes it B-snap and not B-strict:** contrast against a fixed ground is monotone in lightness and the sweep covers the whole range, so a compliant answer exists for every hue (**exercised at 5° steps around the wheel, not asserted**). Where chroma cannot survive at the required lightness the gamut mapper gives up **chroma**, holding lightness and hue — that concession IS the snap, and it means the product never tells a paying customer their brand colour is unusable. **THE EVIDENCE THE TARGETS ENCODE THE SYSTEM AND NOT ONE AUTHOR'S TASTE, and it is the strongest thing in the PR: fed Teal's own hue the engine independently re-derives `--mds-accent-teal-600` (`#1B5E5E`) and `--mds-accent-teal-50` (`#E6F2F2`) BYTE-IDENTICALLY, and returns §4.1 rows 1–3 as 7.48 / 9.40 / 12.10.** Targets are **ratios, not ramp steps**, because the two shipped accents *disagree* about steps (dark Blueprint darkens on hover 6.14→9.14→13.00; dark Teal lightens then darkens 6.68→4.82→9.40, itself exceptions-log #6) and *agree* about ratios; the engine's targets are their midpoint, so a tenant ramp lands in the product's own visual register rather than scraping the 4.5 floor. Two roles are **aliases** drawn from both accents unanimously (light `fg` = light `bg`; dark `ring` = dark `fg`) and a third, light `ring` = light `bg_hover`, is where they disagree and is recorded as a choice. **ONE CONSTRAINT DELIBERATELY OMITTED AND THE OMISSION LOOKS LIKE AN OVERSIGHT: fill-versus-canvas.** A button ought to be distinguishable from the page, and WCAG 1.4.11 is the obvious authority — but measuring the shipped system BEFORE writing any code showed **both ratified accents FAIL a 3:1 reading of it in dark mode (Blueprint 2.61, Teal 2.40)**. Adding it would have made the engine stricter than the design system it serves and rejected the product's own colours. §4.1 does not list it; neither does the engine (ADR-0014 §D6). **DUAL-ENGINE, and three implementation choices exist ONLY to serve parity — each a deviation from what one would otherwise write:** (1) **`x ** (1/3)`, never `Math.cbrt`** — cbrt is the BETTER function, correctly rounded where `pow` is not, and that is exactly why it is wrong: PHP has none, so using it would have the two engines computing one quantity by two routes agreeing only to within a few ulp; **matching the WEAKER implementation is what makes the pair exact**. (2) **Fixed trip counts** (a 1001-point lightness scan, a 32-step gamut bisection), never a tolerance-terminated loop, which can take different iteration counts on two platforms and land on opposite sides of an 8-bit rounding boundary. (3) **Clamp, THEN round** — `Math.round` is half-up, PHP's `round()` is half-away-from-zero, and they agree only on non-negative values. **PHP STAYS AUTHORITATIVE** because four of the five consuming surfaces are server-rendered, and **three of them cannot resolve a CSS custom property at all** (mail clients strip `<style>` and ignore `var()`; dompdf supports neither custom properties reliably nor `oklch()`) — which is also the real reason the derived ramp is **STORED rather than re-derived on read**, with `engine_version` making a future target change an explicit, auditable re-derivation instead of a silent repaint of every live tenant. **THE FIXTURE LIVES IN `tests/fixtures/`, NOT `tests/golden/`** — the H21a-A6 precedent that `condition-serializer.json` and `step-projection.json` already follow: no `grammar_version` key, no manifest entry, so **296 sites and 114 vectors are unmoved** (verified; `git diff tests/golden` empty). Its 12 vectors are chosen by **failure mode**, not coverage: an achromatic trio that must produce ONE ramp (divergence = the engine started reading the input's lightness), a maximally saturated yellow that must snap, a chroma at 2.4× the cap, and near-black/near-white vectors *with a hue* straddling the sRGB transfer function's 0.04045 branch. Each engine **re-measures all seventeen pairings from the STORED hexes** rather than trusting the fixture's ratios — comparing stored ratios only would let a fixture hand-edited to green a red build pass both halves. **DOCS: ADR-0014 + five reconciliations.** DSR §2.9's picker prohibition is **NARROWED, not deleted** — it still governs USER personalization (`AccentToken` stays closed at two) and no longer governs TENANT branding, two layers with two rules, stated once so a future reader does not "restore consistency" by collapsing them. **THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN SOFTENED, in the ADR, the exceptions-log and the DSR alike: the accessibility guarantee moves from STRUCTURAL (no reachable combination CAN be inaccessible, because a human enumerated them all) to PROCEDURAL (every stored ramp was verified at write time) — which is precisely the risk §2.9 was written to close.** Also: exceptions-log **#7**; §4.1 marked as an **executable specification** (its 17 rows ARE `pairings()`, asserted by count and by a 9/8 per-theme split); **§395's absence-as-default invariant amended** for the Blueprint-escape defect H23a3 must close (once a tenant ramp occupies `:root`, absence of `data-accent` stops meaning "product default" and starts meaning "inherit my org's brand", leaving a member no way back — fixed by emitting an explicit `data-accent="blueprint"` only when the tenant has a ramp); `testing-strategy.md`'s dual-engine section; the PRD ADR index. **Gates: Pest 2240 (+39), full suite green; Vitest 1177 (+49) across 54 files; Pint + vue-tsc clean; controller-gate / migration-lint / job-payload-lint green; `composer audit` + `npm audit --omit=dev` clean at push time. PHPStan exactly 55, zero introduced, VERIFIED PER FILE — it read 56 first and THE 56TH WAS MINE**, exactly as this tracker predicts: an unnarrowable `$target['fg']` on a union of two array shapes, now spelled `self::TARGETS['dark']['fg']`. **No schema change, no route change, no `openapi.json` drift, no frontend build change.**

- **H22b (as-built, MERGED PR #92 `84c1034`, 6/6 CI green first run) — the custom-domain ADMIN UI, and `is_primary` with it.** H-map row 256 (`ui, S–M`), shipped **full-stack M/L** and the widening is recorded rather than hidden (the H6b/H21a precedent): **three decisions locked with the user up front — (1) its OWN page `/domains` + a sidebar item** (the /webhooks · /integrations · /analytics operator activated and can never produce one. **ITS DIRECT CONSEQUENCE IS THE EASIEST THING IN THIS INCREMENT TO GET WRONG:** `deactivate()` MUST clear the flag in the same write, or `domains:activate --deactivate` becomes a constraint violation instead of a deactivation — the operator's "take it offline now" would fail. `ActivateCustomDomainCommandTest` pins it, and `TenantHostTest` pins the consequence (the public host falls back to the next-oldest live domain rather than nowhere). **`default false` IS SAFE HERE FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON §D4 REFUSED A `status` DEFAULT:** false is the FAIL-CLOSED value — it means "no preference expressed", so `TenantUrl::publicHost()` falls through to the pre-existing oldest-activated tiebreak (KEPT, not replaced, with `is_primary DESC` merely prepended) and every row that predates the column emits the host it emitted yesterday. **The first activation elects a primary; the second does not** — a one-domain tenant should not have to choose between one thing and nothing, and repointing outstanding respondent links is the tenant's call, never a side effect of an operator running a command. **`TenantUrl::publicHost()`/`appHost()` are now PUBLIC and the presenter READS them** rather than re-deriving "which host do respondents get": `is_public_host` is not simply `is_primary` (a tenant with no preference still has a public host), so a second implementation would label the right row today and the wrong one the first time the fallback mattered. **Net-new:** `App\Http\Controllers\Tenant\DomainController`, `App\Services\Tenancy\DomainPresenter`, `App\Http\Requests\Tenant\StoreDomainRequest` (a SEPARATE class from the `Api\V1` twin — a web surface importing from a versioned namespace makes an API bump a UI change — but composing the SAME `ClaimableDomain`, so what may be claimed and what routes cannot drift), `resources/js/Pages/domains/Index.vue` + `components/domains/{DomainCard,DnsRecordBlock,DomainSetupGuide,types}`, five web routes, one API twin (`POST /api/v1/domains/{domain}/primary`), and the migration. **THE HONESTY IS THE FEATURE:** there is NO activate button, not even a disabled one (that would imply the tenant is one permission away from it), the `verified` badge reads **"Awaiting setup"** rather than "Verified" (a tenant told only "verified" will reasonably repoint live traffic at an origin holding no certificate — the exact failure §D5's TXT-over-CNAME ordering exists to prevent), and the three `DomainVerificationFailure` cases render as three DIFFERENT instructions because they call for three different actions. **§D9's ASYMMETRY IS NOW FULLY HONOURED, WHICH IT WAS NOT BEFORE:** index + destroy carry no `feature:` gate, but the nav item does — so a tenant downgraded off Business would have had no destination at all. `/settings` therefore links `/domains` whenever the tenant actually HOLDS a custom domain (one CONVERGES (the H24b2 precedent; every other seeder block is `doesntExist()`-guarded and drifts), one pending + one awaiting-operator — and **NEITHER ACTIVATED, which is a constraint on the fixture rather than a gap in it**: an activated row is visible to `Domain`'s global scope and would repoint every resume link in the e2e database onto a hostname the browser cannot resolve, failing the
